5.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Andhra Pradesh's rural female casual-labour share of 40.2% was higher, not lower, than India's 18.7%.
5.tq: Use the comparison direction as the trap while retaining the two correct numerical statements.
5.sec: Universal angles

6.s: The expression ‘Hindu rate of growth’ was used to describe India’s economic performance during which period?
6.x: The expression referred to India’s stagnant annual growth during the 1950s to 1980. The trend was considered to have been broken in the 1980s.
6.tq: Use the period associated with the concept rather than confusing it with the year of coining.
6.sec: Hindu rate of growth - who coined it, year, variable, period

6.s: The annual growth rate associated with the ‘Hindu rate of growth’ primarily referred to:
o: Per capita GDP growth of about 3.5%
6.x: The expression referred to annual real GDP growth of approximately 3.5%, or 3.52% for 1950–1980.
6.tq: Distinguish the aggregate real GDP variable from per capita GDP and nominal growth.
6.sec: Hindu rate of growth - who coined it, year, variable, period

6.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s growth during the period associated with the Hindu rate of growth:
1. Real GDP grew at about 3.5% annually.
2. Per capita GDP grew at about 1.37% annually.
3. The growth rate was only marginally above the rate of population growth.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: All three statements are correct. Low real GDP growth translated into per capita growth of only about 1.37%, barely above population growth.
6.tq: Check whether the statements refer consistently to aggregate and per capita growth.
6.sec: Hindu rate of growth - who coined it, year, variable, period

6.s: The growth rate of the Indian economy during the 1980s, which marked a break from the earlier Hindu rate of growth, was approximately:
6.x: India’s growth accelerated to approximately 5.1–5.5% during the 1980s, breaking the earlier stagnant pattern.
6.tq: Use the range and eliminate figures belonging to the earlier or later growth phases.
6.sec: Hindu rate of growth - who coined it, year, variable, period

6.s: A proposed ‘Bharat rate of growth’ associated with AI-led ‘Reforms 3.0’ envisages sustained growth of:
6.x: The proposed Bharat rate of growth refers to growth of 8% or more through AI-led Reforms 3.0.
6.tq: Identify the exact target figure rather than substituting the historical Hindu rate of growth.
6.sec: Hindu rate of growth - who coined it, year, variable, period

6.s: Which one of the following years recorded the lowest GDP growth rate in India since 1961, according to the figures cited?
6.x: The lowest growth rate since 1961 was recorded in 1979, at approximately –5.2%.
6.tq: Distinguish the historical lowest year from other years that also recorded negative growth.
6.sec: GDP growth rate by decade - 1950-51, highest and lowest years

6.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
6.x: Growth in 1990–91 was 1.1%; it fell below 1% during the crisis year 1991–92. Growth was around 5% in 1992–94 and 6.3% in 1994–95.
6.tq: Find the correctly matched year and figure among closely spaced economic data.
6.sec: GDP growth rate by decade - 1950-51, highest and lowest years

b. Second Plan

i. 2.2%
ii. 3.6%
iii. 3.69%
iv. 4.21%

Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer.

6.s: On the eve of independence, which one of the following combinations is correct regarding India’s socio-economic conditions?
o: Per capita income about Rs 1,000, life expectancy 50 years and literacy above 30%
Per capita income about Rs 265, life expectancy 50 years and literacy above 25%
Per capita income about Rs 500, life expectancy 32 years and literacy above 30%
Per capita income about Rs 265, life expectancy 32 years and literacy below 16%
6.x: Per capita income was approximately Rs 265, life expectancy was 32 years and literacy was below 16% on the eve of independence.
6.tq: Test the complete data combination rather than an isolated indicator.
6.sec: Economy on the eve of independence - colonial legacy, livelihood, challenges

6.s: Which of the following statements regarding the occupational structure of India on the eve of independence is correct?
o: More than 75% of workers were employed in industry, which contributed approximately 50% of GDP.
More than 75% of workers depended on agriculture, which contributed approximately 50% of GDP.
Agriculture employed about 50% of workers but contributed over 75% of GDP.
Less than one-fourth of workers depended on agriculture, which contributed nearly 50% of GDP.
6.x: Over 75% of workers depended on agriculture, while agriculture generated approximately 50% of GDP.
6.tq: Match the employment share with the GDP share and reject reversed proportions.
6.sec: Economy on the eve of independence - colonial legacy, livelihood, challenges

6.s: Which of the following best explains the colonial ‘drain of wealth’ mentioned in relation to India?
o: India’s export earnings were invested mainly in Indian capital goods.
British trade policy eliminated all Indian exports.
India’s imports were financed entirely through domestic taxation.
India’s export surplus was spent on Britain’s office and war expenses.
6.x: The export surplus generated by India was used for Britain’s office expenses and war expenses, contributing to the drain of wealth.
6.tq: Identify the mechanism of the drain rather than a general consequence of colonialism.
6.sec: Economy on the eve of independence - colonial legacy, livelihood, challenges

6.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Basic and capital goods — approximately one-fourth of industrial output
Suez Canal — tightened British control over trade
Public sector before independence — steel, automobiles and aviation as its principal areas
6.x: Before independence, the public sector was limited mainly to railways, power, communications and ports. It did not principally cover all the industries listed in option d.
6.tq: Find the option that extends a limited colonial public sector beyond its stated scope.
6.sec: Economy on the eve of independence - colonial legacy, livelihood, challenges

6.s: Which of the following received top priority in the First Plan in response to the immediate economic challenges after independence?
o: Heavy engineering, automobiles and export subsidies
6.x: Large foodgrain imports and inflation led the First Plan to give top priority to agriculture, irrigation and power. Post-partition stabilisation was another immediate challenge.
6.tq: Link the policy priority with the immediate food and inflation problem.
6.sec: Economy on the eve of independence - colonial legacy, livelihood, challenges

6.s: The principal policy orientation of India between 1947 and 1991 was:
o: Import substitution with a substantial public-sector role
Free trade with minimal state intervention
6.x: The major policy orientation was import substitution supported by state planning and public investment, rather than export promotion or deregulation.
6.tq: Distinguish the dominant policy orientation from its deliberately stated alternatives.
6.sec: Policy orientation 1947-1991 - import substitution, licence-permit regime

6.s: Which Plan adopted import substitution as the industrialisation strategy?
6.x: The Third Plan made import substitution the industrialisation strategy.
6.tq: Match the policy strategy with the Plan in which it was formally adopted.
6.sec: Policy orientation 1947-1991 - import substitution, licence-permit regime

6.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956:
1. It was described as the ‘Economic Constitution’.
2. Schedule A contained 17 industries reserved for the state.
3. Schedule B contained 12 industries.
4. Industries outside these schedules could operate in the private sector subject to licensing.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: All four statements are correct. The 1956 Industrial Policy Resolution created the framework associated with the Licence-Permit-Quota Raj.
6.tq: Verify each component of a policy framework before selecting the comprehensive code.
6.sec: Policy orientation 1947-1991 - import substitution, licence-permit regime

6.s: The Bombay Plan is significant because it showed that:
o: Industrialists opposed all forms of state intervention.
The state transferred all industries to foreign companies.
The private sector demanded abolition of industrial licensing in 1944.
Industrialists themselves sought state protection and planning support.
6.x: The Bombay Plan of 1944 was prepared by industrialists who themselves sought state protection, making the Licence Raj partly a capitalist demand.
6.tq: Avoid the common reversal that state planning was opposed by all industrialists.
6.sec: Policy orientation 1947-1991 - import substitution, licence-permit regime

6.s: Which of the following was characteristic of India’s economic policy during the 1980s?
o: Exclusive emphasis on import substitution without any policy change
Reduction of the MRTP asset limit to Rs 10 crore
A shift described as ‘pro-business, not pro-market’
6.x: The 1980s saw a pro-business, not pro-market orientation, including broad-banding of licences, tax cuts, NRI deposits and a higher MRTP limit.
6.tq: Use the exact policy description and check it against the accompanying measures.
6.sec: Policy orientation 1947-1991 - import substitution, licence-permit regime

6.s: Which one of the following changes formed part of the 1991 economic reforms?
o: Expansion of licensing to all private industries
Reduction of public-sector reserved industries from 17 to 8 and delicensing
Replacement of delicensing by compulsory state ownership
Increase in public-sector reserved industries from 8 to 17
6.x: In 1991, the number of industries reserved for the public sector was reduced from 17 to 8, and delicensing was introduced.
6.tq: Watch for reversed numerical changes and identify the reform-oriented combination.
6.sec: Policy orientation 1947-1991 - import substitution, licence-permit regime

6.s: The Incremental Capital-Output Ratio (ICOR) is defined as:
o: Change in capital divided by change in output
Change in output divided by change in capital
6.x: ICOR is the change in capital divided by the change in output. It measures the additional investment needed to produce one additional unit of output.
6.tq: Keep the numerator and denominator in the correct order.
6.sec: Low growth despite high savings - capital-output ratio (ICOR)

6.s: Which of the following statements about ICOR is correct?
o: A higher ICOR always indicates more efficient investment.
A lower ICOR indicates that more capital is needed for one unit of output.
A lower ICOR indicates more efficient investment.
ICOR is unrelated to the efficiency of investment.
6.x: A lower ICOR means that less additional capital is required to generate one additional unit of output, indicating greater investment efficiency.
6.tq: Apply the meaning of the ratio instead of reversing its efficiency implication.
6.sec: Low growth despite high savings - capital-output ratio (ICOR)

6.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Second Plan:
1. Investment was raised from 7% to 11% of national income.
2. Emphasis was placed on heavy and capital-intensive industries.
3. Long gestation periods contributed to a high ICOR.
4. The high ICOR helped keep growth lower than expected.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: All four statements are correct. Although investment increased from 7% to 11%, capital-intensive industries with long gestation periods resulted in a high ICOR and relatively low growth.
6.tq: Connect investment volume, investment composition, gestation period and growth outcome.
6.sec: Low growth despite high savings - capital-output ratio (ICOR)

6.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the stated current indicator?
o: Gross fixed capital formation — approximately 30% of GDP
Net household financial savings — approximately 11% of GDP
Net household financial savings — approximately 30% of GDP
Gross fixed capital formation — approximately 5.3% of GDP
6.x: Gross fixed capital formation was approximately 30% of GDP, while net household financial savings were approximately 5.3% of GDP.
6.tq: Separate the investment indicator from the household-saving indicator and compare their magnitudes.
6.sec: Low growth despite high savings - capital-output ratio (ICOR)

6.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Nationalisation of 14 banks
B. Rupee devaluation
C. Introduction of the Green Revolution
D. Launch of ‘Garibi Hatao’
6.x: Rupee devaluation occurred in June 1966, the Green Revolution began in the mid-1960s, bank nationalisation took place in July 1969, and ‘Garibi Hatao’ was launched in 1971.
6.tq: Fix the dated events first, then place the mid-1960s event before 1969.
6.sec: Chronology of economic milestones and crises

6.s: The Third Plan failed and was followed by the Plan Holiday of 1966–69 mainly in the context of:
o: The East Asian financial crisis and the Covid-19 pandemic
The second oil shock and the 1991 balance-of-payments crisis
Bank nationalisation and the Green Revolution
Wars with China and Pakistan and severe droughts
6.x: The wars of 1962 and 1965, along with severe droughts in 1965–66, contributed to the failure of the Third Plan and the Plan Holiday of 1966–69.
6.tq: Match the crisis with its immediate historical consequences rather than a later economic shock.
6.sec: Chronology of economic milestones and crises

6.s: Rupee devaluation in June 1966 was undertaken in the context of:
o: Balance-of-payments stress after war and drought
6.x: The June 1966 devaluation occurred amid balance-of-payments stress caused by war and drought conditions.
6.tq: Link the policy action to its contemporaneous external-sector cause.
6.sec: Chronology of economic milestones and crises

6.s: The immediate economic objective associated with the nationalisation of 14 banks in July 1969 was to:
o: Extend credit to agriculture and priority sectors
6.x: Bank nationalisation was intended to direct credit towards agriculture and priority sectors.
6.tq: Identify the intended policy impact rather than the institutional action alone.
6.sec: Chronology of economic milestones and crises

6.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
6.x: The 1991 crisis was a balance-of-payments crisis, with foreign exchange reserves sufficient for only about two weeks of imports. The East Asian financial crisis caused the slowdown of 1997–98.
6.tq: Separate similar-looking crisis years by identifying their distinct causes.
6.sec: Chronology of economic milestones and crises

6.s: Which of the following correctly describes the 1991 balance-of-payments crisis?
o: The crisis led to the continuation of the pre-1991 licensing regime without reform.
Foreign exchange reserves covered about two years of imports and the fiscal deficit was 2%.
Foreign exchange was available for only about two weeks of imports and the fiscal deficit was 8.4% in 1990.
The crisis was caused exclusively by the Covid-19 pandemic.
6.x: In 1991, foreign exchange reserves were sufficient for only about two weeks of imports, while the fiscal deficit had reached 8.4% in 1990. The crisis led to the July 1991 LPG reforms.
6.tq: Combine the reserve position, fiscal figure and reform consequence in one crisis profile.
6.sec: Chronology of economic milestones and crises

6.s: The ‘Garibi Hatao’ programme is associated with which leader and objective?
6.x: Indira Gandhi used the slogan ‘Garibi Hatao’ in 1971, and poverty removal became the goal associated with the Fifth Plan.
6.tq: Match the political slogan with its leader and policy objective.
6.sec: Chronology of economic milestones and crises

6.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the major growth contractions mentioned for India?
o: The 1979 contraction was linked to drought and the second oil shock, whereas the 2020–21 contraction was linked to Covid-19.
The 1979 contraction was caused by Covid-19, whereas the 2020–21 contraction was caused by drought.
Both contractions were caused by the East Asian financial crisis.
Both contractions were caused exclusively by balance-of-payments stress.
6.x: The 1979–80 contraction of about 5.2% was associated with drought and the second oil shock. The 2020–21 contraction of about 5.8% resulted from the Covid-19 pandemic.
6.tq: Compare the two negative-growth episodes by their causes and figures.
6.sec: Chronology of economic milestones and crises

6.s: During which period was the average annual growth rate of the Indian economy approximately 3.5 per cent, commonly expressed as 3.52 per cent?
6.x: The average annual growth rate during 1950–1980 was approximately 3.5 per cent, or 3.52 per cent.
6.tq: Use the phase boundaries to distinguish the closely associated growth rates.
6.sec: Phases of Indian development - boundaries and average growth

6.s: The average annual growth rate of the Indian economy during 1980–81 to 1989–90 was approximately:
6.x: The average growth rate during 1980–81 to 1989–90 was in the range of 5.13 to 5.18 per cent.
6.tq: Match the numerical range with the correct development phase.
6.sec: Phases of Indian development - boundaries and average growth

6.s:
With reference to the post-reform period of the Indian economy, consider the following statements:
1. The average growth rate during the 1990s–2010s was approximately 6.5 per cent.
2. Growth was 6.8 per cent from 1993–94.
3. The economy recorded a peak growth rate of 8.5 per cent during 2003–08.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: All three statements are correct. Post-reform growth averaged approximately 6.5 per cent, was 6.8 per cent from 1993–94, and peaked at 8.5 per cent during 2003–08.
6.tq: Check each figure against its associated post-reform period before selecting the coded combination.
6.sec: Phases of Indian development - boundaries and average growth

6.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the growth rates in the post-Covid period according to the new 2022–23 series?
o: 7.7 per cent in 2023–24, 7.2 per cent in 2024–25 and 7.1 per cent as the 2025–26 projection
7.2 per cent in 2023–24, 7.1 per cent in 2024–25 and 7.7 per cent as the 2025–26 projection
7.2 per cent in 2023–24, 7.7 per cent in 2024–25 and 7.1 per cent as the 2025–26 projection
7.1 per cent in 2023–24, 7.2 per cent in 2024–25 and 7.7 per cent as the 2025–26 projection
6.x: The figures are 7.2 per cent for 2023–24, 7.1 per cent for 2024–25 and 7.7 per cent as the 2025–26 projection.
6.tq: Discriminate between similar figures by preserving their chronological order.
6.sec: Phases of Indian development - boundaries and average growth

6.s:
Consider the following statements regarding growth during the Plan era:
1. The overall annual growth during Plans I to XI was approximately 4.5 per cent.
2. The corresponding annual growth before Independence was approximately 1 per cent.
3. Agricultural growth during the Plan era was approximately 2–3 per cent, compared with 0.3 per cent before Independence.
4. Industrial growth during the Plan era was approximately 6–8 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: All four statements are correct. Plan-era growth was about 4.5 per cent annually, compared with about 1 per cent before Independence; agriculture grew by 2–3 per cent and industry by 6–8 per cent.
6.tq: Test the comparison table as a whole, including both aggregate and sectoral figures.
6.sec: Phases of Indian development - boundaries and average growth

6.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Growth before Independence — approximately 1 per cent annually
Industry during the Plan era — approximately 0.3 per cent growth
Agriculture during the Plan era — approximately 2–3 per cent growth
Plans I–XI — approximately 4.5 per cent annual growth
6.x: Industrial growth during the Plan era was approximately 6–8 per cent, not 0.3 per cent. The figure of 0.3 per cent refers to agricultural growth before Independence.
6.tq: Find the sectoral figure wrongly transferred from the comparison table.
6.sec: Phases of Indian development - boundaries and average growth

6.s: Who argued in 2004 that India’s growth transition began around 1980 because of a pro-business, rather than pro-market, attitudinal shift?
o: Dani Rodrik and J. Bradford DeLong
J. Bradford DeLong and Angus Maddison
Arvind Subramanian and J. Bradford DeLong
6.x: Dani Rodrik and Arvind Subramanian argued in 2004 that the growth transition began around 1980 with a pro-business attitudinal shift.
6.tq: Match the economists with the year and the specific interpretation of the turning point.
6.sec: Turning-point debate - 1980s acceleration vs 1991

6.s: J. Bradford DeLong’s 2003 interpretation of India’s economic growth was that:
o: India’s take-off came in the 1980s, before the 1991 reforms
The 1980s growth was entirely caused by agricultural expansion
India’s growth remained close to 1 per cent until 2003
India’s take-off occurred only after the 1991 reforms
6.x: J. Bradford DeLong argued in 2003 that India’s economic take-off occurred in the 1980s, before the 1991 reforms.
6.tq: Separate the pre-1991 take-off interpretation from the alternative 1991 turning-point view.
6.sec: Turning-point debate - 1980s acceleration vs 1991

6.s:
Consider the following statements about the debate on India’s growth turning point:
1. One interpretation places the beginning of the growth transition around 1980.
2. Another interpretation views 1980s growth as debt-fuelled and unstable.
3. Internal borrowing and short-term external commercial borrowings contributed to the instability of the 1980s growth.
4. The fiscal deficit reached 8.4 per cent by 1990.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: All four statements correctly describe the two sides of the turning-point debate and the fiscal and borrowing conditions associated with the 1980s.
6.tq: Combine the competing interpretations with the supporting numerical and borrowing evidence.
6.sec: Turning-point debate - 1980s acceleration vs 1991

6.s: According to the interpretation that identifies 1991 as the decisive turning point, the 1980s growth phase ended with:
o: a sharp decline in agricultural growth alone
the peak growth of 8.5 per cent during 2003–08
the adoption of the new 2022–23 GDP series
6.x: The 1980s growth phase is viewed as debt-fuelled and unstable, and it ended in the 1991 economic crisis. This interpretation identifies 1991 as the turning point to sustained high growth.
6.tq: Link the claimed cause of instability with the event that marked the end of the phase.
6.sec: Turning-point debate - 1980s acceleration vs 1991

6.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the current growth estimates for 2026–27:
1. Real GDP growth in the first quarter of 2026–27 is estimated at 7.8 per cent.
2. Real GVA growth in the first quarter of 2026–27 is estimated at 8.2 per cent.
3. Nominal GDP growth in the first quarter of 2026–27 is estimated at 10.3 per cent.
4. The RBI expects growth for 2026–27 to slow to 6.6 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: All four statements are correct: real GDP is 7.8 per cent, real GVA is 8.2 per cent, nominal GDP is 10.3 per cent for Q1 2026–27, and the RBI expects annual growth to slow to 6.6 per cent.
6.tq: Keep real GDP, real GVA, nominal GDP and the RBI forecast distinct while checking the figures.
6.sec: Universal angles

6.s: Which one of the following correctly states the indicators reported for the first quarter of 2026–27?
o: Real GDP 10.3 per cent, real GVA 7.8 per cent and nominal GDP 8.2 per cent
Real GDP 8.2 per cent, real GVA 10.3 per cent and nominal GDP 7.8 per cent
Real GDP 7.8 per cent, real GVA 10.3 per cent and nominal GDP 8.2 per cent
Real GDP 7.8 per cent, real GVA 8.2 per cent and nominal GDP 10.3 per cent
6.x: The reported figures are 7.8 per cent for real GDP, 8.2 per cent for real GVA and 10.3 per cent for nominal GDP.
6.tq: Split the options by matching each growth figure with the correct national-accounting indicator.
6.sec: Universal angles

6.s: Which of the following is identified as a criticism of India’s recent growth pattern?
o: A complete absence of growth in the tertiary sector
Job-poor growth accompanied by youth unemployment of approximately 10 per cent
Agricultural growth remaining permanently below 0.3 per cent
A universal inability of urban households to afford two meals a day
6.x: Job-poor growth and youth unemployment of approximately 10 per cent are identified as important criticisms. The other statements introduce claims not associated with the stated criticism.
6.tq: Identify the accurately framed criticism without extending it into an absolute claim.
6.sec: Universal angles

6.s: The HCES 2023–24-related concern cited for rural India is that approximately what proportion of rural people cannot afford two thali meals a day?
6.x: The stated concern is that approximately 50 per cent of rural people cannot afford two thali meals a day.
6.tq: Select the reported proportion rather than substituting the nearby unemployment figure.
6.sec: Universal angles

6.s: Ex-CEA Arvind Subramanian estimated India’s growth during 2011–17 at approximately:
o: 4.5 per cent rather than 7 per cent
8.5 per cent rather than 7 per cent
6.5 per cent rather than 4.5 per cent
3.5 per cent rather than 6.8 per cent
6.x: Arvind Subramanian placed India’s growth during 2011–17 at approximately 4.5 per cent, rather than the reported 7 per cent.
6.tq: Discriminate between the alternative growth estimates for the same period.
6.sec: Universal angles

6.s:
With reference to Andhra Pradesh’s growth performance, consider the following statements:
1. Andhra Pradesh outgrew India in most years since 2014–15.
2. In 2025–26, Andhra Pradesh recorded 9.88 per cent growth compared with India’s 7.4 per cent.
3. Andhra Pradesh’s growth was lower than India’s in 2025–26.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Andhra Pradesh’s 9.88 per cent growth was higher than India’s 7.4 per cent in 2025–26.
6.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap to distinguish Andhra Pradesh’s growth from India’s growth.
6.sec: Universal angles

6.s:
Arrange the following average growth rates of Andhra Pradesh in chronological order:
A. 11.3 per cent during 2024–26
B. 13.5 per cent during 2014–19
C. 10.3 per cent during 2019–24
6.x: The chronological sequence is 13.5 per cent during 2014–19, 10.3 per cent during 2019–24 and 11.3 per cent during 2024–26.
6.tq: Arrange the periods first, then attach each growth figure to its corresponding period.
6.sec: Universal angles

6.s: Which of the following correctly represents the sequence of Andhra Pradesh growth figures cited for the successive periods?
o: 13.5 per cent → 10.3 per cent → 11.3 per cent
10.3 per cent → 13.5 per cent → 11.3 per cent
13.5 per cent → 11.3 per cent → 10.3 per cent
11.3 per cent → 10.3 per cent → 13.5 per cent
6.x: The sequence is 13.5 per cent for 2014–19, 10.3 per cent for 2019–24 and 11.3 per cent for 2024–26.
6.tq: Preserve the chronological sequence while comparing the three state-level growth figures.
6.sec: Universal angles

7.s: The Planning Commission of India came into being along with which Budget?
7.x: The Planning Commission was formally set up on 15 March 1950 and came into being with the Budget for 1950–51.
7.tq: Use the closely spaced financial years as the numerical trap.
7.sec: Planning Commission - resolution year, chairman, deputy chairman, status

7.s: The establishment of the Planning Commission in 1950 was recommended by the Advisory Planning Board headed by
7.x: The Advisory Planning Board of 1946, headed by K.C. Neogi, recommended the establishment of the Planning Commission.
7.tq: Match the recommendation with the correct committee chairman.

7.s: Who was the first Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission?
7.x: Gulzarilal Nanda was the first Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission; M.S. Ahluwalia was its last Deputy Chairman.
7.tq: Discriminate between the first and last office-holders.
7.sec: Planning Commission - resolution year, chairman, deputy chairman, status

7.s: Who was the last Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission?
7.x: M.S. Ahluwalia was the last Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission before it was replaced by NITI Aayog.
7.tq: Test the end-point of an office-holder sequence.
7.sec: Planning Commission - resolution year, chairman, deputy chairman, status

7.x: The Planning Commission was modelled on the Soviet Gosplan planning organisation.
7.tq: Identify the institutional model rather than the institutional status.
7.sec: Planning Commission - resolution year, chairman, deputy chairman, status

7.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the position of the Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission?
o: A Cabinet-minister-rank functionary and de facto head of the Commission
A constitutional authority with voting rights in the Cabinet
A representative nominated by the State Governments
A Secretary-rank officer appointed by the Finance Commission
7.x: The Deputy Chairman was the de facto head of the Planning Commission, held Cabinet-minister rank and attended Cabinet meetings without a vote.
7.tq: Separate rank, functional headship and voting power.
7.sec: Planning Commission - resolution year, chairman, deputy chairman, status

7.s: Which of the following was NOT a component of the Planning Commission's regular composition?
o: A Member-Secretary drawn from the senior IAS

9.s: According to the wage-goods model, the principal constraint on economic expansion is the supply of

9.s: How would an increase in the supply of wage goods help the economy according to the wage-goods model?

It would reduce the labour force available for production.

9.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the wage-goods model from the Mahalanobis model?
o: The wage-goods model prioritised heavy industry, whereas the Mahalanobis model prioritised wage goods.
The wage-goods model prioritised agriculture and wage goods, whereas the Mahalanobis model prioritised heavy industry.
Both models gave identical priority to agriculture and heavy industry.
Neither model considered the availability of goods relevant to growth.
9.x: The wage-goods model favoured agriculture and wage goods, while the Mahalanobis strategy gave priority to heavy industry and capital goods.
9.tq: Compare the contrasting sectoral priorities directly.

9.s: The Janata Party came to power at the Union level in 1977 during which Five Year Plan?

9.s: Which of the following correctly represents the broad significance of the three major plan models in India’s planning experience?

10.s:
Consider the following statements about the Mahalanobis model:
1. It assumed a relatively closed economy.
2. It gave priority to capital-intensive heavy industry.
3. It generated substantial employment in the short run.
4. It was associated with food shortages and inflation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
10.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Capital-intensive heavy industry was criticised for creating relatively few jobs, so statement 3 is false.
10.tq: Locate the employment statement that contradicts the capital-intensive strategy.
10.sec: Second Plan - pruning of outlay, criticism of the Nehru-Mahalanobis strategy  [APPSC]

10.s: The Tenth Plan model projected growth of 8.1 per cent, whereas the actual growth during the Plan years lay in the range of:
10.x: The Tenth Plan model projection was 8.1 per cent, while actual growth during the Plan years ranged from 6.2 to 8.6 per cent.
10.tq: Compare the projected figure with the actual range.
10.sec: Second Plan - pruning of outlay, criticism of the Nehru-Mahalanobis strategy  [APPSC]

10.s: Which of the following is an example of duplication during plan implementation?
o: Separate population policies for every district
Parallel Five Year Plans for each ministry
10.x: Duplication in implementation was illustrated by overlapping rural electrification schemes.
10.tq: Apply the concept of duplication to the concrete example.
10.sec: Second Plan - pruning of outlay, criticism of the Nehru-Mahalanobis strategy  [APPSC]

10.s: Which one of the following correctly states the Eighth Plan’s performance against its targets?
o: Public-sector outlay share was 39% against a target of 37%, and employment growth was 4% against 2.6%.
Public-sector outlay share was 45.2% against a target of 34.3%, and employment growth was 2.6% against 2%.
Public-sector outlay share was 25% against a target of 34.3%, and employment growth was 1% against 2%.
Public-sector outlay share was 34.3% against a target of 45.2%, and employment growth was 2% against 2.6%.
10.x: The Eighth Plan achieved a public-sector share of 34.3 per cent against a target of 45.2 per cent, while employment growth was 2 per cent against the target of 2.6 per cent.
10.tq: Read actual and target figures in the correct direction.
10.sec: Second Plan - pruning of outlay, criticism of the Nehru-Mahalanobis strategy  [APPSC]

10.s: The Prakasam Barrage and Nagarjuna Sagar projects are associated respectively with which plan periods?
o: First to Second and First to Second
10.x: Prakasam Barrage, completed in 1957, and Nagarjuna Sagar are both associated with the First-to-Second Plan period.
10.tq: Match project chronology with the plan period rather than the completion year alone.
10.sec: AP projects launched plan-wise  [APPSC]

10.s: Which project was sanctioned during the Third Plan?
10.x: Srisailam was sanctioned in 1963 during the Third Plan.
10.tq: Use the project’s sanction year to identify the plan.
10.sec: AP projects launched plan-wise  [APPSC]

10.s: The foundation stone of Nagarjuna Sagar was laid by Jawaharlal Nehru on:
10.x: Jawaharlal Nehru laid the foundation stone of Nagarjuna Sagar on 10 December 1955.
10.tq: Test the exact date and associated national leader.
10.sec: AP projects launched plan-wise  [APPSC]

10.s: Telugu Ganga is associated with which Five Year Plan?
10.x: The Telugu Ganga project, associated with 1983, was launched during the Sixth Plan.
10.tq: Link the project year with the corresponding plan period.
10.sec: AP projects launched plan-wise  [APPSC]

10.s: The Third Five Year Plan was adversely affected primarily by which combination of events?
o: The 1966 devaluation and the abolition of the Planning Commission
The 1990–91 balance-of-payments crisis and political instability
The 1971 war and the oil shock of 1973
The 1962 and 1965 wars and the 1965–66 drought
10.x: The Third Plan was derailed by the wars of 1962 and 1965 and the severe drought of 1965–66. This led to the Plan Holiday during 1966–69.
10.tq: Use the cause-effect link and distinguish the events responsible for the Plan Holiday.
10.sec: Plans cut short or terminated early

10.s: The postponement of the Eighth Five Year Plan was mainly associated with
o: political instability and the balance-of-payments crisis of 1990–91
the termination of the Fifth Plan by the Janata government
10.x: Political instability and the 1990–91 balance-of-payments crisis postponed the Eighth Plan. Annual Plans were implemented during 1990–92.
10.tq: Match the plan with its specific interruption rather than with a nearby plan crisis.
10.sec: Plans cut short or terminated early

10.s: During the Eleventh Five Year Plan period in Andhra Pradesh, which sector received the first priority?
10.x: The social sector received the first priority in Andhra Pradesh during the Eleventh Plan. Education received the highest priority within the social sector.
10.tq: Identify the broad priority before narrowing it to the highest-priority component.
10.sec: AP Five Year Plans - outlay priority, agriculture share, programmes  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

10.s: Which one of the following was the highest-priority component within the social sector of Andhra Pradesh during the Eleventh Plan?
10.x: Education was given the highest priority within the social sector in Andhra Pradesh during the Eleventh Plan.
10.tq: Test the inner ranking within a broad sector priority.
10.sec: AP Five Year Plans - outlay priority, agriculture share, programmes  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

10.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh during the Eleventh Five Year Plan:
1. The State targeted a GSDP growth rate of 9.5 percent.
2. The State achieved a GSDP growth rate of 5.28 percent.
3. The State achieved an industrial growth rate of 10 percent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
10.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The industrial growth target was 10 percent, but the achievement was 7.26 percent, making statement 3 false.
10.tq: Separate targets from achievements and reject the statement that converts a target into an achievement.
10.sec: AP Five Year Plans - outlay priority, agriculture share, programmes  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

10.s: The industrial growth target and achievement of Andhra Pradesh during the Eleventh Plan were, respectively,
10.x: Andhra Pradesh targeted 10 percent industrial growth during the Eleventh Plan and achieved 7.26 percent.
10.tq: Read the pair in the stated order—target first and achievement second.
10.sec: AP Five Year Plans - outlay priority, agriculture share, programmes  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

10.s: At the end of the Eleventh Five Year Plan, the per capita income of Andhra Pradesh was approximately
10.x: The per capita income of Andhra Pradesh at the end of the Eleventh Plan was ₹68,970, which was above the national figure.
10.tq: Use the exact numerical figure and distinguish it from nearby income values.
10.sec: AP Five Year Plans - outlay priority, agriculture share, programmes  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

10.s: What was the share of agriculture and allied activities in the GSDP of Andhra Pradesh at the end of the Eleventh Plan?
10.x: Agriculture and allied activities accounted for 21.27 percent of Andhra Pradesh’s GSDP at the end of the Eleventh Plan.
10.tq: Test the exact percentage from a comparison of closely spaced numerical options.
10.sec: AP Five Year Plans - outlay priority, agriculture share, programmes  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

10.s: Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) was launched by the Centre in
10.x: RKVY was launched by the Centre in 2007. An allocation of ₹1,862 crore was associated with the programme in the stated account.
10.tq: Use the year-based direct recall pattern for a centrally launched programme.
10.sec: AP Five Year Plans - outlay priority, agriculture share, programmes  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

10.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Jalayagnam in Andhra Pradesh?
o: An irrigation mission launched in 2004 to complete major and medium projects
A financial inclusion scheme launched in 2015
A rural employment programme launched in 1990
An industrial corridor launched in 2007 to promote exports
10.x: Jalayagnam was an irrigation mission launched in Andhra Pradesh in 2004 for completing major and medium irrigation projects.
10.tq: Use the programme-purpose-year combination and reject swapped programme identities.
10.sec: AP Five Year Plans - outlay priority, agriculture share, programmes  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

10.s: Plan finance of a State consists principally of
o: State’s own resources and Normal Central Assistance
Finance Commission grants and private foreign investment
Only tax revenue collected by the Union Government
Only market borrowings and external assistance
10.x: Plan finance comprises the State’s own resources—such as balance from current revenue, public-sector surpluses and borrowings—along with Normal Central Assistance.
10.tq: Combine the two components instead of selecting one source alone.
10.sec: AP plan finance - central assistance, state resources, grouping  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

10.s:
Which of the following are included in the State’s own resources for plan finance?
1. Balance from current revenue
2. Public-sector surpluses
3. Borrowings
4. Normal Central Assistance
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
10.x: Balance from current revenue, public-sector surpluses and borrowings are State’s own resources. Normal Central Assistance is a separate component of plan finance.
10.tq: Separate State-generated resources from central assistance.
10.sec: AP plan finance - central assistance, state resources, grouping  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

10.s: The Gadgil formula for allocation of Central assistance was introduced in
10.x: The Gadgil formula was introduced in 1969. It was later modified into the Gadgil–Mukherjee formula in 1991.
10.tq: Distinguish the original formula year from the later modified formula year.
10.sec: AP plan finance - central assistance, state resources, grouping  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

10.s: Under the Gadgil–Mukherjee formula, which component carried the largest weight in allocating Central assistance?
10.x: Population carried the largest weight of 60 percent. Per capita income had 25 percent, while fiscal performance and special problems had 7.5 percent each.
10.tq: Find the largest weight in a multi-part formula before considering the smaller components.
10.sec: AP plan finance - central assistance, state resources, grouping  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

10.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the Gadgil–Mukherjee formula:

List-I (Component)
a. Population
b. Per capita income
c. Fiscal performance
d. Special problems

List-II (Weight)
i. 7.5 percent
 ii. 25 percent
 iii. 60 percent
 iv. 7.5 percent

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
10.x: Population received 60 percent, per capita income 25 percent, and fiscal performance and special problems received 7.5 percent each.
10.tq: Start from the sure pair with the largest numerical weight and eliminate codes.
10.sec: AP plan finance - central assistance, state resources, grouping  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

10.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the pattern of assistance to States?
o: Special Category States — 90 percent grant and 10 percent loan
General Category States — 90 percent grant and 10 percent loan
Special Category States — 30 percent grant and 70 percent loan
10.x: Special Category States received assistance in the ratio of 90 percent grant and 10 percent loan. General Category States received 30 percent grant and 70 percent loan.
10.tq: Compare the two categories through their grant-loan ratios.
10.sec: AP plan finance - central assistance, state resources, grouping  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

10.s: Andhra Pradesh was classified under which category for the pattern of Central plan assistance?
10.x: Andhra Pradesh was classified as a General Category State. The General Category pattern consisted of 30 percent grant and 70 percent loan.
10.tq: Apply the category classification to the specific State named in the question.
10.sec: AP plan finance - central assistance, state resources, grouping  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

10.s: Which one of the following statements regarding planning institutions is correct?
o: Planning Commission plan grants continued unchanged after 2015.
NITI Aayog retained the Planning Commission’s power to allocate plan funds.
Planning Commission plan grants ended after its abolition in 2015, and NITI Aayog has no fund-allocation role.
NITI Aayog was established to approve State Five Year Plans.
10.x: The abolition of the Planning Commission in 2015 ended its plan-grant role. NITI Aayog does not perform the function of allocating plan funds.
10.tq: Reject the familiar but incorrect transfer of the Planning Commission’s fund-allocation power to NITI Aayog.
10.sec: AP plan finance - central assistance, state resources, grouping  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

10.s: The average growth during the First to Eleventh Five Year Plans was approximately
o: 1 percent, compared with 4.5 percent before Independence
2.5 percent, compared with 3 percent before Independence
4.5 percent, compared with 1 percent before Independence
8 percent, compared with 4.5 percent before Independence
10.x: Average growth during the First to Eleventh Plans was approximately 4.5 percent, compared with about 1 percent in the pre-Independence period.
10.tq: Read the comparison in the stated order and avoid reversing the planning and pre-Independence figures.
10.sec: Achievements of planning - industrial base, food, institutions  [GROUP-II]

10.s: Which range correctly represents the approximate average growth rates of agriculture and industry during the planning period?
10.x: Agriculture grew at approximately 2–3 percent, while industry grew at approximately 6–8 percent during the planning period.
10.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap between agricultural and industrial growth ranges.
10.sec: Achievements of planning - industrial base, food, institutions  [GROUP-II]

10.s: Which of the following groups contains only industrial and scientific institutions associated with the expansion of India’s industrial base during planning?
o: FCI, NABARD, SBI and the Green Revolution
Bhilai, Durgapur, Rourkela and the IITs
NITI Aayog, Gadgil formula, SBI and FCI
10.x: Bhilai, Durgapur and Rourkela steel plants, along with Chittaranjan, Perambur and the IITs, formed part of the industrial and scientific base created during planning.
10.tq: Identify the group belonging to the same institutional-industrial category.
10.sec: Achievements of planning - industrial base, food, institutions  [GROUP-II]

10.s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with India’s achievement of food self-sufficiency during the planning period?
o: Food Corporation of India established in 1965
10.x: The Atomic Energy Commission contributed to scientific and technological capacity, not directly to food self-sufficiency. The Green Revolution, FCI and National Seeds Corporation were associated with food security.
10.tq: Find the institution that belongs to the industrial-scientific group rather than the food-security group.
10.sec: Achievements of planning - industrial base, food, institutions  [GROUP-II]

10.s: The State Bank of India originated from which institution during the First Plan period?
10.x: The State Bank of India was created from the Imperial Bank during the First Plan period.
10.tq: Test the institutional predecessor rather than the later development role.
10.sec: Achievements of planning - industrial base, food, institutions  [GROUP-II]

10.s: NABARD was established in
10.x: NABARD was established in 1982 as one of the important institutions associated with planned development.

10.sec: Achievements of planning - industrial base, food, institutions  [GROUP-II]

10.s: The poverty ratio declined from 48.3 percent in 1977–78 to which level in 1983–84?
10.x: The poverty ratio declined from 48.3 percent in 1977–78 to 37.4 percent in 1983–84.
10.tq: Track the direction and exact end value of a numerical trend.
10.sec: Achievements of planning - industrial base, food, institutions  [GROUP-II]

10.s:
Consider the following statements about the failures of planning:
1. Poverty and inequality persisted.
2. Employment growth lagged behind targets.
3. Regional imbalance existed both across and within States.
4. Industrial growth exceeded targets in every Plan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
10.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because industrial growth remained below target in several Plans, including the Sixth Plan.
10.tq: Find the single absolute statement that overstates a generally uneven planning outcome.
10.sec: Failures - poverty, unemployment, regional imbalance  [GROUP-II]

10.s: The expression “the poor became poorer” was used in relation to which Five Year Plan context?
o: The Eighth Plan’s poverty and safety-net outcomes
The Twelfth Plan’s regional planning strategy
10.x: The expression was used to describe persistent poverty and inequality under the Eighth Plan despite the existence of a safety net.
10.tq: Link the quoted evaluative phrase with the correct Plan context.
10.sec: Failures - poverty, unemployment, regional imbalance  [GROUP-II]

10.s: Which of the following was identified as a continuing regional problem requiring attention under the Twelfth Plan?
o: Excessive industrial concentration only in Union Territories
Regional imbalance across and within States
10.x: Correcting regional imbalance across States and within States was identified as an objective under the Twelfth Plan.
10.tq: Apply the stated planning objective to the regional-development problem.
10.sec: Failures - poverty, unemployment, regional imbalance  [GROUP-II]

10.s: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 and Viksit Bharat 2047?
o: Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 is aligned with Viksit Bharat 2047.
Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 replaced the National Development Council.
Viksit Bharat 2047 is a district-level programme under Swarna Andhra.
Both are annual plans prepared by the Planning Commission.
10.x: Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 is aligned with the national Viksit Bharat 2047 vision and represents a long-horizon development framework for Andhra Pradesh.
10.tq: Test the relationship between two similarly structured development visions.
10.sec: Universal angles

10.s: Which one of the following correctly states the current status of Five Year Plans and plan-style planning?
o: Five Year Plans ended in 2017, but plan-style credit and regional planning continue.
Five Year Plans ended in 2015 and all forms of regional planning also ended.
Five Year Plans continued beyond 2017 under NITI Aayog with unchanged fund allocation powers.
Five Year Plans were replaced by Annual Plans administered by the Planning Commission.

10.tq: Separate the end of a formal planning system from the continuation of planning-like activities.

10.x: The NABARD Andhra Pradesh State Focus Paper 2026–27 proposed a credit plan of ₹5.11 lakh crore, up from ₹4.24 lakh crore.

10.sec: Universal angles

10.s: Under the NABARD Andhra Pradesh State Focus Paper 2026–27, which sector received a proposed allocation of ₹2.55 lakh crore?
10.x: ₹2.55 lakh crore was proposed for agriculture and allied activities, while ₹1.64 lakh crore was proposed for MSMEs.
10.tq: Match the precise allocation with the correct sector rather than the total plan size.
10.sec: Universal angles

10.s: Under Swarna Andhra @2047, which of the following is NOT one of the three economic regions identified for Andhra Pradesh?
10.x: The three identified economic regions are Visakhapatnam, Amaravati and Tirupati. Kurnool is not included in this three-region grouping.
10.tq: Find the outsider in a closed list of three named regions.
10.sec: Universal angles

10.s: With the help of NITI Aayog, the Visakhapatnam economic region under Swarna Andhra @2047 is associated with an envisaged economy of approximately
10.x: The Visakhapatnam economic region is associated with an envisaged economy of USD 750–800 billion by 2047, with NITI Aayog’s assistance.
10.tq: Use the exact range and avoid confusing it with a single-point estimate.
10.sec: Universal angles

10.s: Which one of the following statements about Kerala’s current planning practice is correct?
o: Kerala’s Gender Budget is less than one-tenth of plan outlay.
Kerala continues Annual Plans, and its Gender Budget exceeds one-fifth of plan outlay.
Kerala has completely discontinued Annual Plans.
Kerala uses only Five Year Plans administered by NITI Aayog.
10.x: Kerala continues to prepare Annual Plans, and its Gender Budget accounts for more than one-fifth of plan outlay. Extreme poverty in Kerala was reported to have ended in November 2025.
10.tq: Combine two linked current facts and reject the absolute discontinuation claim.
10.sec: Universal angles

10.s: Kerala was reported to have ended extreme poverty in
10.x: Kerala was reported to have ended extreme poverty in November 2025.
10.tq: Test the precise month and year of a current development milestone.

11.s: The First Five-Year Plan achieved an actual growth rate of approximately:
11.x: The First Plan achieved 3.6 per cent growth against its target of 2.1 per cent.

11.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Plan Holiday:
1. Only Annual Plans were implemented during this period.
2. The Green Revolution began during 1966–67.
3. The Third Plan recorded growth of 5.6 per cent against a target of 2.2 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
11.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 reverses the figures: Third Plan growth was 2.2 per cent against a target of 5.6 per cent.
11.tq: Split the actual-growth and target figures before selecting the coded option.
11.sec: Plan holiday - years and cause

11.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Planning and the Poor — Padma Desai
India: Planning for Industrialization — B.S. Minhas alone
Planning and the Poor — B.S. Minhas
India: Planning for Industrialization — Gulzarilal Nanda
11.x: B.S. Minhas authored Planning and the Poor in 1974. India: Planning for Industrialization was co-authored by Padma Desai and Jagdish Bhagwati.
11.tq: Start from the sure author–work pair and eliminate swapped authors.
11.sec: Critiques of Indian planning → author

11.s:
Padma Desai is associated with which of the following descriptions?
1. She was a well-known critic of India’s planned economy.
2. She was the first Asian woman to earn a PhD in Economics from Harvard.
3. She co-authored India: Planning for Industrialization with Jagdish Bhagwati.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
11.x: All three statements are correct. Padma Desai earned her Harvard Economics PhD in 1960 and co-authored the 1970 work with Jagdish Bhagwati.
11.tq: Use the all-inclusive option when each biographical and authorship detail is supported.
11.sec: Critiques of Indian planning → author

11.s: The chief drawback of Indian planning identified in the context of its implementation was:
11.x: The chief drawback was implementation failure, even though planning produced several measurable achievements.
11.tq: Distinguish a structural implementation problem from an exaggerated claim of complete failure.
11.sec: Critiques of Indian planning → author

11.s: Which of the following was NOT an achievement associated with planning in India?
11.x: Regional disparities persisted and therefore were a failure rather than an achievement. Planning did contribute to savings, investment, food security and scientific manpower.
11.tq: Find the item that belongs to the failures column rather than the achievements column.
11.sec: Achievements vs failures of planning

11.s: Which one of the following was a failure of planning in India?
o: Expansion of transport and irrigation infrastructure
Growth of information technology and space capabilities
11.x: Rising unemployment was identified as a failure and as a root cause of poverty. The other options represent achievements.
11.tq: Separate positive structural outcomes from persistent social failures.
11.sec: Achievements vs failures of planning

11.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Land reforms were poorly implemented.
2. Income inequality was reduced substantially after the reforms.
3. Unequal land ownership persisted.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
11.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because income inequality was not reduced and became wider after the reforms.
11.tq: Use the reversed-trend trap in the statement on inequality.
11.sec: Achievements vs failures of planning

11.s: Average economic growth over Plans I to XI was approximately:
11.x: Average growth over Plans I to XI was about 4.5 per cent, compared with roughly 1 per cent before Independence.
11.tq: Compare the long-period planning average with the pre-Independence benchmark.
11.sec: Achievements vs failures of planning

11.s: Which of the following correctly represents the broad sectoral growth pattern during the plan period?
o: Industry grew by 6–8 per cent and agriculture by 2–3 per cent annually.
Industry grew by 2–3 per cent and agriculture by 6–8 per cent annually.
Both industry and agriculture grew by 6–8 per cent annually.
Both industry and agriculture grew by 0.3 per cent annually.
11.x: Industry grew by about 6–8 per cent, whereas agriculture grew by about 2–3 per cent. Agricultural growth before Independence had been only about 0.3 per cent.
11.tq: Check the reversed comparison between industry and agriculture.
11.sec: Achievements vs failures of planning

11.s: The Fourth Five-Year Plan followed which strategy in relation to growth and self-reliance?
o: Bombay Plan strategy of abandoning public investment
Mahalanobis strategy of complete import dependence
Green Revolution strategy of zero industrial growth
Gadgil strategy of growth with stability
11.x: The Fourth Plan followed the Gadgil strategy, which emphasised growth with stability and progress towards self-reliance.
11.tq: Match the plan with its named strategy and reject unrelated policy labels.

11.s:
Consider the following targets of the Fourth Plan:
1. Agriculture growth of 5 per cent a year
2. Industry growth of 8–10 per cent
3. Exports growth of about 7 per cent a year
Which of the statements given above are correct?
11.x: The Fourth Plan targeted 5 per cent annual agricultural growth, 8–10 per cent industrial growth and about 7 per cent annual export growth.
11.tq: Retain the separate numerical targets before testing the combined option.
11.sec: Fourth Plan strategy on foreign account and self-reliance

11.s: The Fourth Plan envisaged ending concessional PL-480 food imports by:
11.x: The Fourth Plan target was to end concessional PL-480 food imports by 1971.
11.tq: Use the specific deadline rather than the beginning or end year of the plan.
11.sec: Fourth Plan strategy on foreign account and self-reliance

11.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Fourth Plan is correct?
o: It achieved 5.7 per cent growth against a target of 3.3 per cent.
It achieved 2.1 per cent growth against a target of 3.6 per cent.
It achieved 8 per cent growth against a target of 10 per cent.
It achieved 3.3 per cent growth against a target of 5.7 per cent.

11.sec: Fourth Plan strategy on foreign account and self-reliance

11.s: Which major banking-related measure was taken during the Fourth Plan period?
o: The Reserve Bank of India was nationalised in 1969.
All private banks were abolished in 1971.
11.x: A positive development during the Fourth Plan period was the nationalisation of 14 banks in 1969.
11.tq: Use the action-and-number combination to avoid the nationalisation–privatisation trap.
11.sec: Fourth Plan strategy on foreign account and self-reliance

11.s:
Under the Gadgil formula, Special Category States initially included:
1. Assam
2. Jammu and Kashmir
3. Nagaland
Which of the statements given above are correct?
11.x: The initial Special Category States under the Gadgil formula were Assam, Jammu and Kashmir, and Nagaland.
11.tq: Test list completeness through the all-inclusive option.

o: 30 per cent grant and 70 per cent loan
70 per cent grant and 30 per cent loan
50 per cent grant and 50 per cent loan
90 per cent grant and 10 per cent loan

(b) Per capita income

(d) Special problems

11.s: Which statement best describes planning after 1991?
o: It ended immediately after the Seventh Plan.
It shifted from directed planning to indicative planning, signalling priority sectors while leaving investment largely to the private sector.
It was made a constitutional requirement for all state governments.
It shifted from indicative planning to complete state direction of private investment.
11.x: After 1991, planning became indicative: it signalled priority sectors while private investment played a larger role. Planning was not a constitutional requirement.
11.tq: Apply the directed-versus-indicative distinction to the role of private investment.
11.sec: Role of planning after 1991 - why indicative planning continued

11.s: Why did Five-Year Plans continue to provide value in a market economy after 1991?
o: They legally compelled every private firm to follow state targets.
They provided a long-term perspective for economic development.
They replaced Finance Commission transfers to the states.
11.x: Five-Year Plans continued to provide a long-term perspective even in a market economy. Planning itself was not constitutionally mandatory.
11.tq: Choose the purpose-based explanation rather than an exaggerated legal power.
11.sec: Role of planning after 1991 - why indicative planning continued

11.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Establishment of the Planning Commission
B. Establishment of the National Development Council
C. Dissolution of the Planning Commission
D. Establishment of NITI Aayog
11.x: The Planning Commission was established in 1950, the National Development Council in 1952, the Planning Commission was dissolved in 2014, and NITI Aayog was established in 2015.
11.tq: Fix the earliest institutional dates first and then place the two successor events.
11.sec: End of the plan era - last plan, abolition, successor

11.s: Which combination correctly describes the institutional shift associated with NITI Aayog?
o: Judicial planning, competitive federalism and abolition of state planning
Top-down planning, fund allocation and reduced state participation
Bottom-up approach, cooperative federalism and a think-tank role
Centralised planning, statutory authority and compulsory private investment
11.x: NITI Aayog marked a shift towards bottom-up planning and cooperative federalism. It functions primarily as a think tank rather than as a fund allocator.
11.tq: Separate the institutional role of a think tank from the former fund-allocation role.
11.sec: End of the plan era - last plan, abolition, successor

11.s: Which statement regarding the National Development Council is correct?
o: It was established in 1952 and its functions have passed to NITI Aayog’s Governing Council, although a formal abolition resolution remains pending.
It was a constitutional body established under the Constitution.
It was formally abolished before the establishment of NITI Aayog.
It replaced NITI Aayog as the principal fund allocator in 2015.
11.x: The National Development Council was established in 1952 and is now inactive. Its functions have passed to NITI Aayog’s Governing Council, but formal abolition is still pending.
11.tq: Watch for the distinction between functional inactivity and formal abolition.
11.sec: End of the plan era - last plan, abolition, successor

11.s: Which sequence correctly represents the replacement documents associated with NITI Aayog?
11.x: The replacement framework consisted of a Fifteen-Year Vision, Seven-Year Strategy and Three-Year Action Agenda.
11.tq: Arrange the documents by their stated time horizons, not by publication order.
11.sec: Replacement documents - 15-year vision, 7-year strategy, 3-year action agenda

11.s: The first Three-Year Action Agenda of NITI Aayog covered which period?
11.x: The first Three-Year Action Agenda covered the period from 2017–18 to 2019–20.
11.tq: Identify the exact coverage period rather than the year in which the framework was requested.
11.sec: Replacement documents - 15-year vision, 7-year strategy, 3-year action agenda

11.s: Under NITI Aayog’s State Support Mission, States are preparing which documents?
11.x: States are preparing State Vision@2047 documents under NITI Aayog’s State Support Mission.
11.tq: Match the official label with its stated target year.
11.sec: Replacement documents - 15-year vision, 7-year strategy, 3-year action agenda

11.s: Which institutional development ended the system of discretionary plan grants in India?
o: Establishment of the National Development Council
Introduction of the Goods and Services Tax
11.x: The abolition of the Planning Commission ended the system of discretionary plan grants. NITI Aayog was not created as a body with comparable financial powers.
11.tq: Identify the institutional change directly linked with the power that was withdrawn.
11.sec: Universal angles

11.s:
Consider the following statements regarding NITI Aayog:
1. NITI Aayog possesses financial powers to redistribute plan grants among States.
2. Its Governing Council primarily coordinates policy among the Centre and the States.
3. The absence of financial powers limits it from functioning as a direct substitute for the Planning Commission in grant allocation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
11.x: Statement 1 is false: NITI Aayog has no financial powers to redistribute plan grants. Statements 2 and 3 are correct because its Governing Council coordinates policy rather than distributing money.
11.tq: Split the options by checking the reversed financial-power claim.
11.sec: Universal angles

11.s:
Assertion (A): The Governing Council of NITI Aayog coordinates policy rather than redistributing plan grants.
Reason (R): NITI Aayog does not possess financial powers for the distribution of such grants.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
11.x: Both statements are true, and the absence of financial powers explains why the Governing Council performs a coordinating role rather than redistributing plan grants.
11.tq: Test whether the institutional limitation directly explains the stated function.
11.sec: Universal angles

11.s: At the 11th meeting of the NITI Aayog Governing Council, which measure was urged by the Prime Minister to promote grassroots planning?
o: Transfer of all plan grants to the Planning Commission
Replacement of regional planning by a single national plan
Abolition of all State-level planning bodies
11.x: The Prime Minister urged States to estimate GDP at the district level so that planning could move from a top-down approach towards grassroots planning.
11.tq: Match the policy suggestion with its intended shift in planning approach.
11.sec: Universal angles

11.s:
With reference to Kerala's decentralised planning initiative, consider the following statements:
1. The People's Plan Campaign was launched on 17 August 1996.
2. It devolved 35–40% of plan outlay to local bodies.
3. The initiative now being discussed is known as “People's Plan 2.0”.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
11.x: All three statements are correct. Kerala's People's Plan Campaign began on 17 August 1996, devolved 35–40% of plan outlay to local bodies, and “People's Plan 2.0” is under discussion.
11.tq: Check the date, percentage and successor label separately before selecting the combined option.
11.sec: Universal angles

11.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Discussion of “People's Plan 2.0” in Kerala
B. Launch of Kerala's People's Plan Campaign
C. Abolition of the Planning Commission and emergence of NITI Aayog
D. The 11th NITI Aayog Governing Council's emphasis on district-level GDP estimates
11.x: The People's Plan Campaign began in 1996, followed by the change from the Planning Commission to NITI Aayog, the 11th Governing Council's district-GDP emphasis, and the later discussion of “People's Plan 2.0”.
11.tq: Fix the earliest dated event first and then place the later planning developments.
11.sec: Universal angles

11.s: Andhra Pradesh currently follows regional planning through which of the following set of economic regions?
11.x: Andhra Pradesh uses regional planning across three economic regions: Visakhapatnam, Amaravati and Tirupati.
11.tq: Discriminate the exact three-member regional grouping from near-looking alternatives.
11.sec: Universal angles

11.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Planning feature)
A. Kerala's People's Plan Campaign
B. Amaravati Economic Region
C. NITI Aayog Governing Council
D. Andhra Pradesh regional planning

List-II (Associated detail)
i. Coordination of policy without redistribution of plan grants
ii. Three economic regions
iii. Nine districts and about 44,962 sq km
iv. Devolution of 35–40% of plan outlay to local bodies

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
11.x: The People's Plan Campaign devolved 35–40% of plan outlay; the Amaravati region covers nine districts and about 44,962 sq km; the NITI Governing Council coordinates policy; and AP has three economic regions.
11.tq: Start from the sure percentage and area pairs, then complete the remaining matches.

12.s: Which of the following sets correctly represents the four principal areas of the mandate of NITI Aayog?
o: Agricultural marketing; customs administration; currency printing; census operations
Knowledge and innovation; NITI for States; driving transformational change; monitoring and evaluation
Fiscal federalism; monetary policy; public debt management; industrial licensing
Defence production; foreign policy; judicial reforms; election management
12.x: The mandate of NITI Aayog covers knowledge and innovation, NITI for States, driving transformational change, and monitoring and evaluation.
12.tq: Match the institution’s mandate with its actual functional areas and reject unrelated governmental functions.
12.sec: NITI Aayog - full form, establishment, mode, status  [APPSC]

12.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Vice-Chairperson from the Chief Executive Officer of NITI Aayog?
o: The CEO is the ex-officio Chairperson, whereas the Vice-Chairperson is nominated by the Finance Commission.
The Vice-Chairperson and the CEO are separate posts; both are appointed by the Prime Minister, but the CEO has a fixed tenure and the rank of Secretary to the Government of India.
The Vice-Chairperson is a constitutional authority, whereas the CEO is a statutory authority.
The Vice-Chairperson is appointed by the President, whereas the CEO is appointed by Parliament.
12.x: The Vice-Chairperson and CEO are distinct offices. The Prime Minister appoints both; the CEO has a fixed tenure and the rank of Secretary to the Government of India.
12.tq: Separate two closely associated offices by comparing their appointing authority and service status.

12.s: Who was the first Chief Executive Officer of NITI Aayog?
12.x: Sindhushree Khullar was the first CEO of NITI Aayog. Amitabh Kant and B.V.R. Subrahmanyam served later as CEOs.
12.tq: Identify the inaugural office-holder rather than the better-known subsequent incumbent.

12.s: Ashok Kumar Lahiri became Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog after replacing:
12.x: Ashok Kumar Lahiri was appointed Vice-Chairperson on 25 April 2026, succeeding Suman K. Bery, who had held the post from May 2022.
12.tq: Use the immediate predecessor trap in questions involving successive office-holders.

12.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Chief Executive Officer of NITI Aayog:
1. The CEO is appointed by the Prime Minister.
2. The CEO holds the rank of Secretary to the Government of India.
3. The tenure of the CEO is fixed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
12.x: All three statements are correct. The CEO is appointed by the Prime Minister, has a fixed tenure and enjoys the rank of Secretary to the Government of India.
12.tq: Check each statement against the appointment, tenure and rank provisions before selecting the combination.

12.s:
Consider the following statements about the composition of NITI Aayog:
1. The number of full-time members is not fixed.
2. Part-time members may be drawn from universities and research institutions.
3. Part-time members are ex-officio and rotational.
4. The maximum number of part-time members is two.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
12.x: All four statements are correct. NITI Aayog has no fixed ceiling for full-time members, while it can have at most two rotational, ex-officio part-time members from universities and research bodies.
12.tq: Combine the general composition rule with the numerical ceiling for part-time members.
12.sec: Composition - full-time, part-time, ex-officio, special invitees  [APPSC]

12.s: The maximum number of ex-officio members in NITI Aayog is:
o: Four Union Ministers nominated by the Prime Minister
Two Union Ministers nominated by the Prime Minister
Five Union Ministers nominated by the Governing Council
Three Union Ministers nominated by the President
12.x: NITI Aayog may have a maximum of four ex-officio members, who are Union Ministers nominated by the Prime Minister.
12.tq: Split the option into number and nominating authority before choosing the correct composition rule.
12.sec: Composition - full-time, part-time, ex-officio, special invitees  [APPSC]

12.s: Special invitees to NITI Aayog are best described as:
o: Domain experts and practitioners nominated by the Prime Minister
Chief Ministers elected by the Governing Council
Members of Parliament selected by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Officials of the Finance Commission nominated by the President
12.x: Special invitees are domain experts and practitioners nominated by the Prime Minister.
12.tq: Identify the correct category and nominating authority instead of confusing special invitees with ex-officio members.
12.sec: Composition - full-time, part-time, ex-officio, special invitees  [APPSC]

12.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the outgoing full-time members of the NITI Aayog panel?
