The Labour Bureau under the Ministry of Labour and Employment
34.x: PLFS is conducted by the National Statistical Office, which functions under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
34.tq: Apply the 'who conducts the survey?' agency test.
34.sec: PLFS - agency, launch, frequency  [APPSC]

34.s: The Standing Committee on Labour Force Statistics was set up on the advice of which body and was associated with the design of PLFS?
34.x: The Standing Committee on Labour Force Statistics was set up on the advice of the National Statistical Commission and designed the PLFS framework.
34.tq: Match the technical committee with the institution that recommended it.
34.sec: PLFS - agency, launch, frequency  [APPSC]

34.s: The Periodic Labour Force Survey was launched in:
34.x: PLFS was launched in April 2017. Its first annual report, relating to 2017–18, was released in May 2019.
34.tq: Distinguish the launch date from the release date of the first report.
34.sec: PLFS - agency, launch, frequency  [APPSC]

34.s: Which of the following correctly describes the original design of PLFS?
o: Only decennial rural estimates under UPS
Quarterly estimates for all areas under CDS alone
Annual rural and urban estimates under UPSS and CWS, with quarterly urban CWS estimates
Monthly all-India CDS estimates and annual urban estimates only
34.x: The original PLFS design provided annual rural and urban estimates under UPSS and CWS, along with quarterly CWS estimates for urban areas.
34.tq: Select the option containing the complete original survey design.
34.sec: PLFS - agency, launch, frequency  [APPSC]

34.s:
Which of the following changes was introduced with the PLFS revamp from January 2025?
1. Monthly all-India CWS estimates began to be produced.
2. Quarterly estimates were extended to rural areas.
3. The annual report shifted to the calendar year January–December.
4. The sample was reduced to about one-half of its earlier size.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The sample was raised, not reduced, to about 2,72,304 households.
34.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the direction of a sample-size change.
34.sec: PLFS - agency, launch, frequency  [APPSC]

34.s: After the January 2025 revamp, the PLFS sample was raised to approximately:
34.x: The revised PLFS sample was raised to approximately 2,72,304 households, described as about 2.65 times the earlier size.
34.tq: Test the exact sample-size figure rather than the approximate multiplier alone.
34.sec: PLFS - agency, launch, frequency  [APPSC]

34.s: Which of the following persons would ordinarily be outside the labour force?
o: A student or homemaker not seeking work
A person unemployed but available for work
34.x: Persons who are not seeking work and are not available for work, such as some students and homemakers, are outside the labour force.
34.tq: Apply the condition of seeking or being available for work.
34.sec: Key labour indicators - LFPR, WPR, UR  [APPSC]

34.s: The Unemployment Rate is calculated as:
o: Employed persons divided by total population multiplied by 100
Unemployed persons divided by labour force multiplied by 100
Unemployed persons divided by total population multiplied by 100
Labour force divided by total population multiplied by 100
34.x: UR measures the unemployed as a percentage of the labour force, not of the entire population. The latter denominator is used for Proportion Unemployed.
34.tq: Separate unemployment rate from proportion unemployed by checking the denominator.
34.sec: Key labour indicators - LFPR, WPR, UR  [APPSC]

34.s: Which agency conducted the quinquennial Employment–Unemployment rounds from the 27th to the 68th Round and has conducted PLFS since 2017?
34.x: The NSSO, now within the NSO, conducted the quinquennial employment-unemployment rounds and became the institutional source for PLFS from 2017.
34.tq: Match the historical survey series with its responsible agency.
34.sec: Agencies and sources of unemployment data  [APPSC]

34.s: Which organisation conducts the Employment–Unemployment Survey and the Quarterly Employment Survey of establishments?
o: Labour Bureau under the Ministry of Labour and Employment
Directorate General of Employment and Training alone
34.x: The Labour Bureau under the Ministry of Labour and Employment conducts the Employment–Unemployment Survey and the Quarterly Employment Survey of establishments.
34.tq: Use the survey title to identify the responsible labour institution.
34.sec: Agencies and sources of unemployment data  [APPSC]

34.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. CMIE — monthly household survey through CPHS
2. DGE&T/Employment Exchanges — registration data of job seekers
3. Census of India — main and marginal worker data every ten years
4. CSO — merged with NSSO into NSO in 2019
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
34.x: All four pairs are correct. CMIE conducts the CPHS, Employment Exchanges provide registration data, Census supplies decennial worker data, and CSO and NSSO were merged into NSO in 2019.
34.tq: Verify each agency-role relationship before choosing the complete combination.
34.sec: Agencies and sources of unemployment data  [APPSC]

34.s: Before the establishment of NITI Aayog, unemployment data were primarily obtained from:
34.x: Before NITI Aayog, unemployment data were primarily obtained from the NSSO. Official unemployment information was also associated with the CSO and NSSO statistical system.
34.tq: Recall the principal historical source rather than a newer private source.
34.sec: Agencies and sources of unemployment data  [APPSC]

34.s: Which statement about CMIE and PLFS is correct?
o: PLFS is a private survey and CMIE is conducted by MoSPI.
CMIE designs PLFS through the Standing Committee on Labour Force Statistics.
CMIE is a private monthly household-survey source, whereas PLFS is the standard NSO mechanism.
Both are decennial official Census exercises.
34.x: CMIE conducts a private monthly household survey through CPHS. PLFS, conducted by NSO, is the standard official mechanism for measuring unemployment in India.
34.tq: Compare agency status, frequency and official character.
34.sec: Agencies and sources of unemployment data  [APPSC]

34.s: According to PLFS 2023–24, the overall unemployment rate in Andhra Pradesh under UPSS was:
34.x: Andhra Pradesh recorded an overall unemployment rate of 4.1% under UPSS in PLFS 2023–24, compared with 3.2% for India.
34.tq: Distinguish the State figure from the corresponding national figure.
34.sec: AP unemployment rate in PLFS

34.s:
Consider the following statements regarding youth unemployment in Andhra Pradesh under PLFS 2023–24:
1. The unemployment rate for youth aged 15–29 was 17.5%.
2. The rural youth unemployment rate was 15.5%.
3. The urban youth unemployment rate was 22.7%.
4. The urban female youth unemployment rate was 29.1%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: All four statements are correct for Andhra Pradesh under PLFS 2023–24. The national youth unemployment rate given for comparison was 10.2%.
34.tq: Check all State-level subcategories before selecting the complete code.
34.sec: AP unemployment rate in PLFS

34.s: The Labour Force Participation Rate and Worker Population Ratio of Andhra Pradesh reported in the relevant PLFS-based State estimates were respectively:
34.x: Andhra Pradesh recorded an LFPR of 47.5% and a WPR of 45.6%. LFPR is higher because it includes both employed and unemployed persons in the labour force.
34.tq: Preserve the indicator order and distinguish LFPR from WPR.
34.sec: AP unemployment rate in PLFS

34.s: Which one of the following comparisons is correct for PLFS 2023–24?
o: Andhra Pradesh overall unemployment was 4.1%, higher than India’s 3.2%.
India recorded 4.1%, while Andhra Pradesh recorded 3.2%.
Andhra Pradesh overall unemployment was lower than India’s rate.
Andhra Pradesh and India both recorded 5.9%.
34.x: Andhra Pradesh recorded 4.1%, while the all-India rate was 3.2%. Thus, the State rate was higher than the national rate.
34.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap carefully when comparing State and national figures.
34.sec: AP unemployment rate in PLFS

34.s: The Dantwala Committee on unemployment estimates was constituted in:
34.x: The Expert Committee on Unemployment Estimates, popularly known as the Dantwala Committee, was constituted in 1970.
34.tq: Separate the years of closely related employment committees.
34.sec: Committees on employment statistics

34.s: What was the principal recommendation of the Dantwala Committee regarding unemployment estimation?
o: To replace NSS surveys with CMIE surveys
To provide separate estimates by status and by category
To use one single national number for all forms of unemployment
34.x: The Dantwala Committee rejected a single-number estimate and recommended separate estimates by usual, weekly and daily status, as well as by category.
34.tq: Identify the committee recommendation that rejects an over-simplified single measure.
34.sec: Committees on employment statistics

34.s: Which committee reviewed unemployment estimates and employment-oriented policies in 1973?
o: Standing Committee on Labour Force Statistics
34.x: The Bhagwati Committee, constituted in 1973, reviewed unemployment estimates and employment-oriented policies.
34.tq: Match the committee with its year and subject of review.
34.sec: Committees on employment statistics

34.s:
Consider the following committees or bodies:
1. Dantwala Committee — separate unemployment estimates by usual, weekly and daily status
2. Bhagwati Committee — employment-oriented policies
3. Standing Committee on Labour Force Statistics — design of PLFS
Which of the above pairs are correctly matched?
34.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. The Dantwala Committee dealt with status-wise estimates, the Bhagwati Committee reviewed employment policies, and SCLFS designed PLFS.
34.tq: Match each committee or body with its distinctive institutional role.
34.sec: Committees on employment statistics

34.s: From which year did India shift to monthly unemployment data based on the Current Weekly Status (CWS) approach?
34.x: India shifted to monthly unemployment data based on the CWS approach from 2025.
34.tq: Use the date-specific recall approach and distinguish the stated year from nearby years.
34.sec: Universal angles

34.s: Under the Current Weekly Status approach, a person is treated as employed if the person worked for at least:
o: Eight hours during the reference week
One hour during the reference week
Seven days during the reference week
One day during the reference week
34.x: Under the CWS approach, working for even one hour during the reference week is sufficient for classification as employed. Critics argue that this may mask underemployment and miss circular migration.
34.tq: Test the precise threshold in a definition and use nearby time periods as distractors.
34.sec: Universal angles

34.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the measurement of unemployment in India:
1. Critics argue that the CWS measure may mask underemployment.
2. Critics argue that the CWS measure may fail to capture circular migration adequately.
3. The CWS measure is regarded as free from all measurement-related limitations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct criticisms of the CWS approach. Statement 3 is false because the approach has been criticised for masking underemployment and missing circular migration.
34.tq: Find the false absolute statement and select the combination containing the two supported criticisms.
34.sec: Universal angles

34.s:
With reference to unemployment in Andhra Pradesh and India during 2024–25, consider the following statements:
1. Andhra Pradesh recorded an unemployment rate of 4.1%.
2. The national unemployment rate was 3.2%.
3. Andhra Pradesh's unemployment rate was below the national rate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: Andhra Pradesh recorded an unemployment rate of 4.1%, while the national rate was 3.2% in 2024–25. Therefore, Statement 3 is false; Andhra Pradesh's rate was above the national rate.
34.tq: Compare the two stated percentages before checking the reversed-comparison trap.
34.sec: Universal angles

34.s: The unemployment rate of Andhra Pradesh in 2024–25 was reported to be driven primarily by:
34.x: The higher unemployment rate in Andhra Pradesh was attributed to urban and youth unemployment.
34.tq: Link the reported rate to its stated causes rather than relying on a generic unemployment explanation.
34.sec: Universal angles

34.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes CMIE data from PLFS data in the measurement of unemployment?
o: CMIE data are monthly, use a larger sample, and differ methodologically from PLFS, contributing to divergence in their estimates.
CMIE and PLFS estimates cannot diverge because both use the same frequency, sample size and methodology.
CMIE data are monthly and based on a larger sample, whereas CMIE and PLFS use identical methodologies.
PLFS data are monthly and use a larger sample, whereas CMIE data are based on the PLFS methodology.
34.x: CMIE data are monthly and based on a larger sample, but CMIE and PLFS use different methodologies. These differences can produce divergence between their unemployment estimates.
34.tq: Split the alternatives by frequency, sample size and methodology to identify the complete comparison.
34.sec: Universal angles

35.s: The term ‘jobless growth’ refers to a situation in which:
o: Employment rises while output remains constant
Economic growth is accompanied by a proportionate rise in employment
Unemployment of labour increases during a period of high economic growth
Economic growth is restricted to the agricultural sector
35.x: Jobless growth describes a situation in which unemployment increases despite high economic growth.
35.tq: Use the precise definition rather than associating growth automatically with employment.

35.s: Who coined the term ‘jobless growth’ in the early 1990s?
35.x: The term ‘jobless growth’ was coined by Nick Perna in the early 1990s.
35.tq: Direct name-recall question using closely related economists as distractors.

35.s: Employment elasticity is expressed as:
o: Percentage change in employment divided by percentage change in output
Percentage change in output divided by percentage change in employment
Total employment divided by total population
Change in labour force divided by change in unemployment
35.x: Employment elasticity equals the percentage change in employment divided by the percentage change in output or GDP.
35.tq: Recall the numerator and denominator of the formula without reversing them.

35.s: A low or nearly zero employment elasticity generally indicates:
o: A rapid expansion of labour-intensive manufacturing
Capital-intensive growth with little employment generation
A decline in GDP accompanied by rising employment
35.x: A low or near-zero employment elasticity means that output growth is generating little additional employment and may signal jobless growth.
35.tq: Apply the elasticity concept to infer the employment outcome.

35.s: Which one of the following was a major reason for jobless growth in India after 1991?
o: Decline in the use of capital-intensive technology
Growth driven largely by capital-intensive sectors such as IT and finance
Complete withdrawal of private investment from services
Dominance of labour-intensive manufacturing over services
35.x: Post-1991 growth was driven substantially by capital-intensive sectors such as IT and finance rather than labour-intensive manufacturing.
35.tq: Identify the correct cause while rejecting the reversed cause-and-effect options.

35.s: The expression ‘missing middle’ in the context of India’s employment pattern refers to:
o: The gap between rural and urban literacy rates
The shortage of middle-level government officials
The absence of a manufacturing stage between agriculture and services
35.x: India followed a services-led path that largely skipped the manufacturing stage, described as the ‘missing middle’.
35.tq: Discriminate between an economic structural term and literal interpretations of the words.

35.s:
Which of the following best explains the employment problem associated with India’s post-1991 growth?
1. Growth of employment did not keep pace with labour-force growth.
2. Employment generation was concentrated sufficiently in labour-intensive manufacturing.
3. Unemployment increasingly appeared in the unorganised sector.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
35.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because growth was not sufficiently concentrated in labour-intensive manufacturing.
35.tq: Find the reversed statement about the sector generating employment.

35.s: Approximately how many persons enter India’s job market each year, as indicated in the cited estimates?
35.x: The cited estimate states that about 12 million persons enter the job market each year.
35.tq: Select the stated demographic magnitude from ascending alternatives.

35.s: The National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector (NCEUS) defined the unorganised sector as comprising:
o: All enterprises employing fewer than 50 workers
Unincorporated private enterprises owned by individuals or households, operating on a proprietary or partnership basis, with fewer than 10 workers
All registered companies without trade unions
Only government-owned enterprises employing casual labour
35.x: NCEUS defined the unorganised sector as unincorporated private enterprises owned by individuals or households, on a proprietary or partnership basis, with fewer than 10 workers.
35.tq: Use the complete institutional definition, including ownership, legal form and worker threshold.

35.s:
Consider the following statements regarding an informal worker:
1. An informal worker may work in the unorganised sector.
2. An organised-sector worker without employment or social-security benefits may also be an informal worker.
3. Informal workers are confined exclusively to unincorporated enterprises.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
35.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because informal employment can also exist within the organised or formal sector.
35.tq: Test the distinction between the unorganised sector and informal employment.

35.s: The presence of contract and outsourced workers within formal enterprises is described as:
35.x: Contract and outsourced hiring within formal enterprises is referred to as ‘informalisation of formal enterprises’.
35.tq: Discriminate between closely related formalisation and informalisation expressions.

35.s: Approximately what proportion of non-agricultural employment was informal according to PLFS 2022–23?
35.x: Non-agricultural informal employment was approximately 78% according to PLFS 2022–23.
35.tq: Recall the employment-share figure and avoid confusing it with the overall informal-worker share.

35.s:
Which of the following statements about informal employment in India is correct?
1. About 90% of workers are informal according to one cited estimate.
2. Another estimate places the share of workers outside structured payroll at nearly 85%.
3. Informal employment exists only in the agricultural sector.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
35.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because informal employment also exists in non-agricultural and formal-sector activities.
35.tq: Combine two compatible estimates and reject the sector-exclusive statement.

35.s: The surveys of unincorporated enterprises conducted under the NSS framework continue as:
o: Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises (ASUSE)
35.x: The continuing survey series is the Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises, or ASUSE, under the NSS framework.
35.tq: Distinguish between similarly named labour and enterprise surveys.

35.s: Under the Code on Social Security, 2020, unorganised workers include:
o: Home-based workers, self-employed workers and wage workers in the unorganised sector
Only casual workers employed by registered companies
35.x: The Code on Social Security, 2020 includes home-based, self-employed and wage workers in the unorganised sector within the category of unorganised workers.
35.tq: Identify the statutory category through its three-part composition.

35.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding the status of workers in India?
o: Urban regular wage or salaried employment — 39.8%
35.x: Self-employment accounted for 55.8%. The cited figures for casual labour and urban regular wage or salaried employment were 18.9% and 49.8%, respectively.
35.tq: Start from the sure percentage pair and eliminate altered figures.
35.sec: Quality of employment - status shares and social security

35.s: According to Q2 FY26, the share of casual labour in the cited employment-status distribution was:
35.x: Casual labour accounted for 18.9% in Q2 FY26.
35.tq: Test the exact percentage with nearby numerical distractors.
35.sec: Quality of employment - status shares and social security

35.s: In Q2 FY26, regular wage or salaried workers constituted what share of urban jobs?
35.x: Regular wage or salaried workers constituted 49.8% of urban jobs in Q2 FY26.
35.tq: Recall the urban-specific share rather than the overall status shares.
35.sec: Quality of employment - status shares and social security

35.s: Which of the following correctly describes the rural–urban pattern of employment?
o: Rural employment is dominated by services, while urban employment is dominated by agriculture
Agriculture accounts for 62.0% of urban employment, while services account for 57% of rural employment
Agriculture accounts for 57% of rural employment, while services account for 62.0% of urban employment
Both rural and urban employment are dominated equally by manufacturing
35.x: Agriculture accounted for 57% of rural employment, whereas services accounted for 62.0% of urban employment.
35.tq: Compare the sectoral leaders in rural and urban employment without reversing them.
35.sec: Quality of employment - status shares and social security

35.s: The India Employment Report 2024 was released jointly by:
o: The IMF and the Labour Bureau
The World Bank and NITI Aayog
The ILO and the Institute for Human Development
The UNDP and the National Statistical Office
35.x: The India Employment Report 2024 was released by the International Labour Organization and the Institute for Human Development.
35.tq: Identify the correct institutional partnership rather than a neighbouring international body.
35.sec: Quality of employment - status shares and social security

35.s: The India Employment Report 2024 highlighted that informal and vulnerable jobs are found even among:
35.x: The report noted that informal and vulnerable employment exists even among educated youth.
35.tq: Test the report’s significant qualification rather than its broad subject.
35.sec: Quality of employment - status shares and social security

35.s: Which statement correctly reflects the employment conditions of Generation Z in the cited data?
o: 14.2% had a formal job contract and 20.1% had some social security
More than half had formal contracts and social security
20.1% had a formal job contract and 14.2% had some social security
Both formal contracts and social security covered 40.1%
35.x: Only 14.2% of Gen Z had a formal job contract, while 20.1% had some social security.
35.tq: Keep the two close percentages attached to their correct indicators.
35.sec: Quality of employment - status shares and social security

35.s: The expression ‘formal informality’ refers to the observation that new EPFO ‘formal’ jobs are often:
o: Permanent, high-wage and exclusively public-sector jobs
35.x: ‘Formal informality’ describes EPFO-recorded formal jobs that may nevertheless be short-term, low-wage or contractual.
35.tq: Distinguish formal registration from the actual quality and security of employment.
35.sec: Quality of employment - status shares and social security

35.s: The Labour Bureau Quarterly Employment Survey covers establishments with at least 10 workers in how many sectors?
35.x: The QES covers establishments with 10 or more workers across nine sectors.
35.tq: Recall the survey’s coverage threshold and number of sectors.

35.s: Which of the following is NOT among the sectors covered by the Labour Bureau Quarterly Employment Survey?
35.x: The listed QES sectors include manufacturing, construction, trade, transport, accommodation and restaurants, IT/BPO, education, health and financial services; mining and quarrying is not listed.
35.tq: Find the sector outside the stated nine-sector coverage list.

35.s:
Which of the following statements regarding employment in agriculture is correct?
1. Agriculture accounted for 42.4% of total employment in Q2 FY26.
2. The rural agriculture share fell from 58.5% to 55.8% between the cited periods in 2026.
3. The rural agriculture share rose from 55.8% to 58.5% during the same period.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
35.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 reverses the reported direction of change.
35.tq: Check both the numerical values and the direction of the trend.

35.s: The number of persons aged 15 years and above employed in Q2 FY26 was approximately:
35.x: Approximately 56.2 crore persons aged 15 years and above were employed in Q2 FY26.
35.tq: Select the employment total from close crore-based alternatives.

35.s: How many new jobs were added over Q1 in Q2 FY26 according to the cited estimate?
35.x: The cited estimate reported 8.7 lakh new jobs over Q1 in Q2 FY26.
35.tq: Recall the quarter-on-quarter addition rather than the total employment figure.

35.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the historical change in agriculture’s workforce share?
35.x: Agriculture’s workforce share declined from 72% in 1951 to 64.75% in 1993–94.
35.tq: Track the direction and dates of a long-term structural change.

35.s:
Arrange the following Female Labour Force Participation Rate figures in chronological order of the PLFS round:
A. 30%
B. 23.3%
C. 32.5%
D. 24.5%
35.tq: Arrange the figures by their PLFS years rather than by numerical size alone.
35.sec: Female LFPR - trend, rural vs urban, feminisation of agriculture

35.s: Which of the following correctly matches the PLFS round with the Female LFPR for persons aged 15 years and above?
35.x: The Female LFPR was 32.8% in 2021–22, 37% in 2022–23 and 41.7% in 2023–24.
35.tq: Start with the exact year–percentage pair and eliminate shifted years.
35.sec: Female LFPR - trend, rural vs urban, feminisation of agriculture

35.s: For 2022–23, which pair correctly represents rural and urban Female LFPR respectively?
35.x: In 2022–23, rural Female LFPR was 41.5% and urban Female LFPR was 25.4%.
35.tq: Keep the rural and urban figures in their correct order.
35.sec: Female LFPR - trend, rural vs urban, feminisation of agriculture

35.s: The Female LFPR for 2023–24 was:
35.x: The Female LFPR for 2023–24 was 41.7%.
35.tq: Identify the year-specific figure from adjacent PLFS values.
35.sec: Female LFPR - trend, rural vs urban, feminisation of agriculture

35.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Female LFPR figures cited for 2025?
35.x: For 2025, the overall Female LFPR was approximately 40%, with 45.9% in rural areas and 27.7% in urban areas.
35.tq: Match the aggregate figure with the correct rural–urban breakdown.
35.sec: Female LFPR - trend, rural vs urban, feminisation of agriculture

35.s: The widening rural–urban gap in Female LFPR is primarily indicated by which of the following?
o: A much larger increase in rural LFPR than in urban LFPR
A decline in rural LFPR and a rise in urban LFPR
Identical rural and urban LFPR levels by 2025
A larger increase in urban LFPR than in rural LFPR
35.x: Rural LFPR rose substantially more than urban LFPR, widening the rural–urban gap.
35.tq: Infer the trend from the comparative changes rather than from a single level.
35.sec: Female LFPR - trend, rural vs urban, feminisation of agriculture

35.s: The quarterly Current Weekly Status Female LFPR for January–March 2026 was:
35.x: The quarterly CWS Female LFPR for January–March 2026 was 34.7%.
35.tq: Distinguish the quarterly CWS figure from annual PLFS figures.
35.sec: Female LFPR - trend, rural vs urban, feminisation of agriculture

35.s: Rural women accounted for approximately what share of the rise in female workers between 2017–18 and 2023–24?
35.x: Rural women accounted for about 80% of the increase in female workers during the period.
35.tq: Recall the contribution share rather than the overall Female LFPR.
35.sec: Female LFPR - trend, rural vs urban, feminisation of agriculture

35.s:
Which of the following factors were identified as drivers of the rise in rural female workers?
1. Subsistence farming
2. Unpaid family work
3. Distress employment

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
35.x: Subsistence farming, unpaid family work and distress employment were all identified as drivers of the rise in rural female workers.
35.tq: Use the complete set of causes when all listed statements are supported.
35.sec: Female LFPR - trend, rural vs urban, feminisation of agriculture

35.s: According to the U-shaped hypothesis, Female LFPR generally:
o: Falls with early income growth and rises later with education and service-sector opportunities
Rises with early income growth and falls with later education
Remains constant regardless of income and education
Falls continuously as service-sector employment expands
35.x: The U-shaped hypothesis proposes that Female LFPR initially falls with income growth and rises later as education and service-sector opportunities expand.
35.tq: Apply the two-stage movement implied by the U-shaped hypothesis.
35.sec: Female LFPR - trend, rural vs urban, feminisation of agriculture

35.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a barrier to women’s labour-force participation?
35.x: Social norms, unpaid care work and unsafe transport are barriers; expansion of service-sector opportunities is associated with increased participation at a later stage.
35.tq: Find the supportive factor among the listed barriers.
35.sec: Female LFPR - trend, rural vs urban, feminisation of agriculture

35.s: Which one of the following best describes the gig economy?
o: Employment of workers exclusively in government departments
Engagement of independent contractors and freelancers instead of permanent workers
Employment based only on hereditary occupations
Permanent employment with guaranteed pension benefits
35.x: The gig economy is based on independent contractors and freelancers rather than permanent workers. Delivery services, ride-sharing and freelancing are common examples.
35.tq: Distinguish the exact meaning of a paired economic term from its misleading permanent-employment alternative.

35.s: Which of the following activities is most closely associated with the gig and platform economy?
o: Regular appointment to a permanent civil service post
Employment under a statutory pension scheme only
35.x: Delivery services, ride-sharing and freelancing are examples of work commonly associated with the gig and platform economy.
35.tq: Apply the definition to a practical employment situation.

35.s: According to NITI Aayog's report titled ‘India's Booming Gig and Platform Economy’, the estimated number of gig workers in India during 2020-21 was
35.x: NITI Aayog estimated 77 lakh gig workers in 2020-21.
35.tq: Separate the base-year estimate from later actual and projected figures.

35.s: NITI Aayog projected that the number of gig workers would reach which of the following levels by 2029-30?
35.x: The NITI Aayog projection was 2.35 crore gig workers by 2029-30, equivalent to about 6.7% of the workforce.
35.tq: Use the time reference to distinguish a long-term projection from current estimates.

35.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the gig economy in India:
1. The gig workforce grew by 55% to about 120 lakh in FY25.
2. The gig workforce accounted for over 2% of the workforce according to the Economic Survey 2025-26.
3. The projected gig workforce for 2025-26 was 2.35 crore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
35.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The projection for 2025-26 was 1.43 crore, while 2.35 crore was the projection for 2029-30.
35.tq: Split the statements by their different time periods before choosing the coded combination.

35.s: The NITI projections cited for the gig workforce in 2024-25 and 2025-26 were respectively
35.x: The cited projections were 1.27 crore for 2024-25 and 1.43 crore for 2025-26.
35.tq: Read paired annual figures in chronological order and reject the long-term projection.

35.s: Under the Code on Social Security, 2020, aggregators are required to contribute what proportion of their annual turnover to a fund for the benefit of gig workers?
35.x: Aggregators contribute 1% to 2% of annual turnover to a fund intended to support life and health insurance and pensions for gig workers.
35.tq: Match the statutory contribution range with its stated social-security purpose.

35.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the measurement and registration of gig workers is correct?
o: PLFS records only platform workers, while e-Shram excludes migrant workers.
PLFS does not yet capture gig workers as a distinct category, and most remain outside e-Shram registration.
PLFS already records gig workers as a separate category and all are registered on e-Shram.
PLFS excludes all informal workers and e-Shram covers only permanent workers.
35.x: The Periodic Labour Force Survey does not yet identify gig workers as a distinct category, and most gig workers remain outside e-Shram registration.
35.tq: Use the contrast between survey classification and portal registration.

35.s: How many central labour laws were merged into four labour codes?
35.x: Twenty-nine central labour laws were consolidated into four labour codes.
35.tq: Distinguish the number of laws from the number of resulting codes.

35.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Labour Code)
 a. Code on Wages
 b. Industrial Relations Code
 c. Code on Social Security
 d. Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code

List-II (Year)
 i. 2019
 ii. 2020
 iii. 2020
 iv. 2020

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
35.x: The Code on Wages was enacted in 2019. The Industrial Relations Code, Code on Social Security, and Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code were enacted in 2020.
35.tq: Start with the unique year pair and then match the three codes carrying the same year.

35.s: The number of sections in the central labour laws was reduced from 1,232 to
35.x: The consolidated labour codes reduced the number of sections from 1,232 to 480.
35.tq: Do not confuse the reduced number of sections with the reduced number of rules.

35.s: The number of rules associated with the central labour laws was reduced from 1,436 to
35.x: The number of rules was reduced from 1,436 to 401.
35.tq: Separate the rules figure from the sections figure by identifying the correct before-and-after pair.

35.s: Labour is placed in which List of the Constitution of India?
35.x: Labour is included in the Concurrent List, allowing both the Union and the States to legislate on the subject.
35.tq: Use the subject classification to discriminate between Union, State and Concurrent powers.

35.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the recent labour-code framework:
1. Draft central rules were released in December 2025.
2. Formalisation is expected to rise from 60.4% to 75.5% by 2029-30.
3. A 1.25% gain in GDP is expected by 2029-30.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
35.x: All three statements are correct: draft central rules were released in December 2025, formalisation is expected to rise to 75.5%, and the projected GDP gain is 1.25% by 2029-30.
35.tq: Check the dates, percentages and projected outcome independently before selecting the combined code.

35.s: The e-Shram portal was launched on
35.x: The e-Shram portal was launched on 26 August 2021.
35.tq: Discriminate between closely related national launch dates.

35.s: Which ministry launched the e-Shram portal?
o: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
35.x: The e-Shram portal was launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment.
35.tq: Apply the ‘who launched it?’ test to distinguish the responsible ministry from related ministries.

35.s: e-Shram is India's first Aadhaar-authenticated
35.x: e-Shram is India's first Aadhaar-authenticated National Database of Unorganised Workers, abbreviated as NDUW.
35.tq: Identify the exact official expansion of the portal's database description.

35.s: The Universal Account Number provided through the e-Shram portal consists of how many digits?
35.x: Each registered worker receives a 12-digit Universal Account Number through e-Shram.
35.tq: Use the number-of-digits clue to distinguish the UAN from other identification numbers.

35.s: Which one of the following persons is eligible for registration on the e-Shram portal, subject to the stated conditions?
o: An income-tax payer aged 40 years who is not an agricultural worker
An agricultural worker aged 18 years who is not an income-tax payer or EPFO/ESIC member
35.x: e-Shram covers unorganised workers aged 16-59, including agricultural workers, but excludes income-tax payers and EPFO or ESIC members.
35.tq: Test eligibility by checking age, occupation and exclusion conditions together.

35.s: Which of the following categories is covered by the e-Shram portal?
o: Only government employees below 59 years of age
Unorganised workers including gig, migrant and agricultural workers
35.x: The portal covers unorganised workers, including gig workers, migrant workers and agricultural workers.
35.tq: Reject the exclusive options and identify the inclusive coverage category.

35.s: The e-Shram One-Stop Solution introduced in 2024 integrates how many welfare schemes?
35.x: The e-Shram One-Stop Solution integrates 15 welfare schemes.
35.tq: Link the numerical figure to the specific one-stop-service feature rather than to total registrations.

35.s: Which of the following schemes can e-Shram registrants join through the integrated welfare framework?
35.x: e-Shram registrants can join PMSBY, PMJJBY and PM-SYM through the integrated welfare framework.
35.tq: Recognise the correct cluster of welfare schemes instead of mixing it with administrative institutions.

35.s: The number of unorganised workers registered on the e-Shram portal has crossed
35.x: Registrations on the e-Shram portal have crossed 31.64 crore unorganised workers.
35.tq: Pay attention to the crore-lakh place value when reading a large registration figure.

35.s:
With reference to female labour force participation in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. The female LFPR for all ages in Andhra Pradesh is 35.8%.
2. The corresponding all-India figure is 31.7%.
3. Andhra Pradesh has a lower female LFPR than India for all ages.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
35.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Andhra Pradesh's all-age female LFPR of 35.8% is higher than India's 31.7%, so statement 3 is false.
35.tq: Check both the figures and the direction of comparison before selecting the code.
35.sec: AP female LFPR and informal workforce

35.s: For persons aged 15 years and above, the female LFPR in Andhra Pradesh and India was respectively
35.x: For the 15-years-and-above population, female LFPR was 44.8% in Andhra Pradesh and 41.7% in India.
35.tq: Match the age group with the correct pair of regional percentages.
35.sec: AP female LFPR and informal workforce

35.s: The overall LFPR in Andhra Pradesh was 47.5%. Its rural and urban components were respectively
35.x: The overall LFPR in Andhra Pradesh was 47.5%, comprising 50.1% in rural areas and 41.3% in urban areas.
35.tq: Identify the two components of the overall rate and avoid confusing LFPR with WPR or informality shares.
35.sec: AP female LFPR and informal workforce

35.s: Which of the following correctly represents the female Worker Population Ratio in Andhra Pradesh?
35.x: The female WPR in Andhra Pradesh was 39.6% in rural areas and 22.8% in urban areas.
35.tq: Keep WPR distinct from LFPR and informal-sector employment shares.
35.sec: AP female LFPR and informal workforce

35.s: The urban female youth Worker Population Ratio in Andhra Pradesh was only
35.x: The urban female youth WPR in Andhra Pradesh was only 15.9%.
35.tq: Identify the youth-specific urban figure rather than the broader urban female WPR.
35.sec: AP female LFPR and informal workforce

35.s: The informal-sector share of employment in Andhra Pradesh was higher in rural areas than in urban areas by approximately
35.x: The rural share was 62.3% and the urban share was 45.6%; the difference was 16.7 percentage points.
35.tq: Subtract comparable rural and urban percentages rather than confusing the result with the overall share.
35.sec: AP female LFPR and informal workforce

35.s: The overall informal-sector share of employment in Andhra Pradesh was approximately
35.x: The overall informal-sector share of employment in Andhra Pradesh was approximately 55%.
35.tq: Distinguish the approximate overall figure from the separate rural and urban shares.
35.sec: AP female LFPR and informal workforce

35.s: Which one of the following comparisons regarding labour-market indicators in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Female LFPR in AP is above the national average, but urban female youth WPR is only 15.9%.
Female LFPR in AP is below the national average, while urban female youth WPR is high.
AP's rural informal employment share is lower than its urban informal employment share.
Both female LFPR and urban female youth WPR in AP are above the national average.
35.x: Andhra Pradesh has a female LFPR above the national average, but its urban female youth WPR is only 15.9%. The rural informal employment share is also higher than the urban share.
35.tq: Combine the direction of comparison with the specific youth indicator and eliminate reversed relationships.
35.sec: AP female LFPR and informal workforce

35.s: According to PLFS 2025, the approximate values of India's LFPR, WPR and unemployment rate were respectively
35.x: PLFS 2025 reported an approximate LFPR of 59%, WPR of 57% and unemployment rate of 3%.
35.tq: Preserve the correct order of the three labour-market indicators before matching the figures.

35.s: The size of India's workforce according to PLFS 2025 was approximately
35.x: India's workforce was reported at approximately 61.6 crore according to PLFS 2025.
35.tq: Distinguish the workforce total from labour-force rates and gig-worker estimates.

35.s: Which change in factory employment was reported for the period 2011-2023?
o: Direct factory employment remained at 61%, while contract workers rose to 47%.
Direct factory employment rose from 47% to 61%, while contract workers fell to 42%.
Direct factory employment fell from 61% to 47%, while contract workers rose to 42%.
Both direct and contract employment fell by 42%.
35.x: Direct factory employment declined from 61% to 47% between 2011 and 2023, while the share of contract workers increased to 42%.
35.tq: Track both directions of change and avoid reversing the two employment categories.

35.s: Which of the following is identified as a reason for urban young women staying out of the labour force in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Higher education and absence of flexible working timings
Excessive availability of permanent factory jobs
Compulsory retirement before the age of 25 years
35.x: Higher education and the lack of flexible working timings are identified as factors keeping urban young women out of the labour force in Andhra Pradesh.
35.tq: Connect the observed labour-market outcome with the stated social and workplace factors.

36.s: The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act was first proposed in 1991 by which of the following persons?
36.x: The National Rural Employment Guarantee legislation was first proposed in 1991 by P. V. Narasimha Rao.
36.tq: Use the person–proposal association rather than the later enactment date.
36.sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

36.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the initial implementation of the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act?
o: It began in 200 districts on 2 February 2006.
It began in 150 most backward districts in 2004.
It began in all districts on 1 April 2008.
It began in 625 districts on 2 October 2009.
36.x: The Act was launched on 2 February 2006 in 200 districts. The all-district coverage was achieved later, from 1 April 2008.
36.tq: Distinguish the initial coverage from later nationwide expansion.
36.sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

36.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the expansion of the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act:
1. An additional 130 districts were covered during 2007–08.
2. All districts were brought under the programme from 1 April 2008.
3. The programme initially covered 625 districts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
36.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the programme initially covered 200 districts; 625 refers to later all-district coverage, not the initial launch.
36.tq: Split the statements by separating initial coverage from later expansion.
36.sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

36.s: The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005, was passed in which month and year?
36.x: The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act was passed in September 2005.
36.tq: Distinguish the enactment date from the launch and renaming dates.
36.sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

36.s: With effect from 1 July 2026, which legislation replaced the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act?
o: National Food for Work Programme Act, 2004
Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025
36.x: The Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025, replaced MGNREGA and came into force on 1 July 2026.
36.tq: Identify the exact official title in a scheme-renaming and replacement question.
36.sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

36.s: Under the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, the guaranteed wage employment and the period over which the programme is operated are respectively:
36.x: VB-G RAM G provides 125 days of employment per household and operates over 305 days.
36.tq: Compare the paired numerical features instead of recalling either number in isolation.
36.sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

36.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025?
o: Funding pattern — Entirely demand-driven Central funding
Seasonal pause — States may pause works for up to 60 days during sowing and harvest
Wage payment — Only once at the end of the financial year
36.x: States may pause works for up to 60 days during sowing and harvest. VB-G RAM G has a 60:40 funding pattern, a 9 per cent administrative cost ceiling and weekly or fortnightly wage payment.
36.tq: Find the one correctly matched feature among swapped policy provisions.
36.sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

36.s: The funding pattern under the VB-G RAM G Act is correctly stated as:
o: Entirely financed by the Central Government
50:50 between Centre and States in all regions
60:40 between Centre and States, with 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States and Union Territories
90:10 between Centre and States in all States
36.x: The general funding pattern is 60:40, while the ratio is 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States and Union Territories.
36.tq: Check the general ratio and its stated regional exception.
36.sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

36.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four priority areas of works under VB-G RAM G?
36.x: The four priority areas are water security, core rural infrastructure, livelihood infrastructure, and extreme-weather or disaster-related works. Urban metro-rail development is not included.
36.tq: Eliminate the option outside the specified four-category framework.
36.sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

36.s: Which one of the following statements about the additional provisions of VB-G RAM G is correct?
o: Contractors are made compulsory for all works.
The statutory wage floor is fixed at ₹250 per day.
Job cards are renamed Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Cards.
Assets are recorded only in NREGASoft.
36.x: Under VB-G RAM G, job cards become Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Cards. The Act prohibits contractors, places assets on the VB-NRIS stack and specifies a statutory wage floor of ₹300 per day.
36.tq: Use exact terminology to distinguish renamed instruments from existing systems.
36.sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

36.s: Under MGNREGA, the unit to which the employment guarantee is attached is:
o: Each adult individual in a rural area
Each registered worker in a Gram Panchayat
36.x: The entitlement under MGNREGA is provided to a household, not separately to every individual adult.
36.tq: Discriminate between the household-based entitlement and an individual-based interpretation.

36.s: Which provision of the Constitution is associated with the right to work that provides the Directive Principles basis for MGNREGA?
36.x: MGNREGA is anchored in Article 41, which relates to the right to work, education and public assistance in certain cases.
36.tq: Match the policy objective with the relevant constitutional article.

36.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the target group and objectives of MGNREGA:
1. It covers rural households whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work.
2. It seeks to reduce distress migration.
3. It is primarily intended for urban skilled workers.
4. It includes natural resource management and durable asset creation among its objectives.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
36.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is false because MGNREGA targets rural households volunteering for unskilled manual work, not urban skilled workers.
36.tq: Identify the target group first, then test the associated objectives.

36.s: Which Ministry is the nodal Ministry for MGNREGA?
o: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
36.x: MGNREGA is administered by the Ministry of Rural Development.
36.tq: Use the ministry–scheme association and avoid neighbouring ministry substitutions.
36.sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

36.s: Which statement regarding wages under MGNREGA is correct?
o: The wage is fixed by Gram Sabhas and paid after one financial year.
The wage is State-specific and notified, and payment is made through Aadhaar-linked accounts by DBT.
The wage is determined by the World Bank and credited to any unregistered account.
The wage is uniform throughout India and is paid only in cash.
36.x: MGNREGA wages are State-specific and notified. They are transferred through DBT to Aadhaar-linked accounts.
36.tq: Ask who fixes the wage and how the payment is transferred.
36.sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

36.s: Wages under MGNREGA are required to be paid within how many days of the work done?
36.x: MGNREGA wages are to be paid within 15 days of the work done. Delay attracts compensation.
36.tq: Use the precise statutory time limit rather than the broader idea of timely payment.
36.sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

36.s: What is the minimum share of women prescribed among MGNREGA beneficiaries?
36.x: At least one-third of MGNREGA beneficiaries must be women, although their actual share has consistently exceeded 50 per cent of person-days.
36.tq: Distinguish the statutory minimum from the actual participation trend.

36.s: Which pair is correctly matched in the context of MGNREGA monitoring?
o: Bhuvan — GeoMGNREGA geo-tagging platform; NREGASoft — Management Information System
Bhuvan — Wage payment authority; NREGASoft — Social audit forum
GeoMGNREGA — Constitutional provision; NREGASoft — Central Finance Commission
NREGASoft — Satellite launch vehicle; Bhuvan — Unemployment allowance portal
36.x: Bhuvan, developed by ISRO, supports GeoMGNREGA geo-tagging, while NREGASoft is the programme's Management Information System.
36.tq: Start from the sure technology–function pair and reject swapped institutional roles.

36.s: Social audit of MGNREGA works is mandatory and is conducted by:
36.x: Social audit is mandatory under MGNREGA and is conducted by the Gram Sabha. Gram Sabhas also plan and monitor works.
36.tq: Identify the local participatory body responsible for the function.

36.s: If employment is not provided within 15 days of an application under MGNREGA, the unemployment allowance is at least:
o: One-fourth of the wage throughout the period
One-fourth of the wage for the first 30 days and one-half thereafter
One-half of the wage for the first 30 days and one-fourth thereafter
The full wage for the first 30 days and one-half thereafter
36.x: The unemployment allowance is at least one-fourth of the wage for the first 30 days and one-half thereafter.
36.tq: Track the change in rate after the first 30-day period.

36.s: Which of the following is an example of convergence under MGNREGA?
o: Replacing Gram Sabha monitoring with private contractors
Providing urban metro employment through the PMRY portal
Providing 90 or 95 person-days to PMAY-G beneficiaries through the AwaasSoft–NREGASoft link
Transferring all MGNREGA works to the Ministry of Commerce
36.x: MGNREGA converges with PMAY-G by providing 90 or 95 person-days to eligible beneficiaries through the AwaasSoft–NREGASoft link.
36.tq: Recognise convergence from the linked scheme and digital platform.

36.s: The annual scale of MGNREGA is broadly represented by which of the following ranges?
36.x: The broad annual scale is about 5–6 crore households and 200–250 crore person-days.
36.tq: Match the two related scale indicators rather than selecting an isolated figure.

36.s: Which one of the following is classified as a self-employment programme rather than a wage-employment programme?
36.x: PMEGP is a self-employment programme. NREP, SGRY and NFFWP are wage-employment programmes.
36.tq: Separate programmes by the nature of employment created, not by their rural focus.

36.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. NREP — Wage employment
2. IRDP — Self-employment
3. MGNREGS — Wage employment
4. NRLM — Wage employment
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
36.x: NREP and MGNREGS are wage-employment programmes, while IRDP is a self-employment programme. NRLM belongs to the self-employment group, so pair 4 is incorrect.
36.tq: Classify each programme before checking the coded combination.

36.s: PMRY, introduced in 1993, was primarily intended for:
36.x: The Prime Minister's Rozgar Yojana, or PMRY, was intended for educated unemployed youth and was a self-employment programme.
36.tq: Link the scheme acronym with its distinctive target group.

36.s: The Food for Work Programme was started in 1977 during the government led by:
36.x: The Food for Work Programme was started in 1977 by the Janata government.
36.tq: Use the year–government association while distinguishing it from NFFWP.

36.s: The National Food for Work Programme was launched on 14 November 2004 in:
o: All 200 districts covered initially by NREGA
36.x: NFFWP was launched on 14 November 2004 in the 150 most backward districts.
36.tq: Retain both the launch date and the precise district count.

36.s: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between NFFWP, SGRY and NREGA?
o: NFFWP and SGRY were created after NREGA in 2009.
NFFWP and SGRY were subsumed into NREGA in its districts from 2006.
Only SGRY was subsumed into NFFWP in 2010.
NREGA was subsumed into SGRY in 2004.
36.x: NFFWP and SGRY were subsumed into NREGA in the districts covered by NREGA from 2006. The 2009 event was the addition of the name Mahatma Gandhi, not the merger of NFFWP.
36.tq: Use the sequence of predecessor programmes and avoid the renaming-year trap.

36.s:
Arrange the following employment programmes in chronological order of their introduction:
A. Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme
B. Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas
C. Jawahar Rozgar Yojana
D. Employment Assurance Scheme
36.x: DWCRA was introduced in 1982, RLEGP in 1983, JRY in 1989 and EAS in 1993. Therefore, the correct order is B, A, C, D.
36.tq: Fix the earliest and latest items first, then place the two middle programmes.

36.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Programme)
a. IRDP
b. NREP
c. DWCRA
d. RLEGP

List-II (Year)
i. 1982
ii. 1978–79
iii. 1980
iv. 1983

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
36.x: IRDP dates from 1978–79, NREP from 1980, DWCRA from 1982 and RLEGP from 1983.
36.tq: Start from the distinctive year associations and eliminate codes with a swapped pair.

36.s: IRDP was extended to all development blocks on:
36.x: IRDP was introduced in 1978–79 and extended to all development blocks on 2 October 1980.
36.tq: Distinguish the programme's initial year from the later nationwide block coverage date.

36.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
36.x: SGRY was introduced in 2001. JRY dates from 1989, SGSY/JGSY from 1 April 1999, and NFFWP from 2004.
36.tq: Find the correctly matched year after checking the neighbouring programme dates.

36.s: Which one of the following correctly states the chronological position of NREGA and VB-G RAM G in the employment-programme sequence?
o: NREGA — 2006; VB-G RAM G — 2025 Act, in force from 1 July 2026
NREGA — 1999; VB-G RAM G — 2025 Act, in force from 1 April 2026
36.x: NREGA dates from 2006. VB-G RAM G is a 2025 Act that came into force on 1 July 2026.
36.tq: Separate the year of enactment from the later date on which the legislation came into force.

36.s: The World Development Report 2014 described MGNREGA as a:
36.x: The World Bank's World Development Report 2014 called MGNREGA a “stellar example of rural development.”
36.tq: Recall the distinctive evaluative phrase and its institutional source.
36.sec: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages  [APPSC]

36.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the ministry and implementing agency associated with the Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)?
o: Ministry of Skill Development; implemented by NSDC
Ministry of Labour and Employment; implemented by NCS
Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises; implemented by KVIC
Ministry of Rural Development; implemented by DRDA
36.x: PMEGP is administered by the Ministry of MSME and implemented by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC).
36.tq: Use the ‘who launched or implements it?’ method to distinguish neighbouring ministries and agencies.

36.s:
With reference to PMEGP, consider the following statements:
1. It supports new non-farm micro-enterprises in both rural and urban areas.
2. The margin-money subsidy generally ranges from 15 per cent to 35 per cent.
3. The maximum project cost is ₹50 lakh for manufacturing and ₹20 lakh for services.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
36.x: All three statements correctly describe PMEGP: its target is new non-farm micro-enterprises, its margin money ranges from 15% to 35%, and its project caps are ₹50 lakh for manufacturing and ₹20 lakh for services.
36.tq: Split the statements into target, subsidy and numerical-limit components before choosing the code.

36.s: PMEGP was formed by integrating which two earlier programmes?
36.x: PMEGP, launched in 2008, was formed by combining the Prime Minister’s Rozgar Yojana (PMRY) and the Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP).
36.tq: Identify the predecessor programmes rather than the ministry or beneficiary group.

36.s: The earlier project-cost limits under PMEGP, before the revised limits, were:
o: ₹50 lakh for manufacturing and ₹20 lakh for services
₹20 lakh for manufacturing and ₹10 lakh for services
₹10 lakh for manufacturing and ₹5 lakh for services
₹25 lakh for manufacturing and ₹10 lakh for services
36.x: The earlier PMEGP limits were ₹25 lakh for manufacturing projects and ₹10 lakh for service projects; the later limits became ₹50 lakh and ₹20 lakh respectively.
36.tq: Compare the older and current numerical limits carefully instead of selecting the larger revised figures automatically.

36.s: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) is primarily associated with:
o: Collateral-free credit for urban street vendors
Formal employment incentives through EPF support
Placement-linked skill development for rural poor youth
36.x: DDU-GKY provides placement-linked skilling for rural poor youth and has its roots in the special projects of SGSY.
36.tq: Match the scheme with its distinctive target group and delivery mechanism.

36.s: Which ministry is associated with DDU-GKY?
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
36.x: DDU-GKY is a programme of the Ministry of Rural Development.
36.tq: Discriminate between schemes serving rural youth, urban vendors and formal-sector employees.

36.s: PM-SVANidhi primarily provides:
o: Long-term housing loans to rural households
Subsidised loans to traditional artisans only
Collateral-free working-capital loans to street vendors
36.x: PM-SVANidhi provides collateral-free working-capital loans to street vendors. The scheme has covered more than 75 lakh vendors.
36.tq: Use the target occupation—street vendors—to separate PM-SVANidhi from other credit schemes.

36.s: PM Vishwakarma is implemented by which ministry and covers how many traditional artisan trades?
o: Ministry of Labour and Employment; 15 trades
36.x: PM Vishwakarma is associated with the Ministry of MSME and covers 18 traditional artisan trades, with training, toolkits and credit support.
36.tq: Combine the ministry clue with the exact count to avoid confusing artisan and skilling schemes.

36.s: Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyan, launched in 2020, was designed as a 125-day campaign for returnee migrant workers in:
36.x: The campaign covered 116 districts in six States and was intended for returnee migrant workers.
36.tq: Read the duration, district count and State count as separate numerical clues.

36.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: National Career Service — Labour and Employment — job-matching portal
Recognition of Prior Learning — Housing and Urban Affairs — street-vendor credit
PM-SVANidhi — Rural Development — rural youth skilling
36.x: The National Career Service belongs to the Labour and Employment domain and functions as a job-matching portal. The other pairs interchange the functions or ministries of different schemes.
36.tq: Start with the sure ministry-function pair and eliminate the swapped combinations.

36.s: The National Career Service had more than how many employers registered?
36.x: The National Career Service had more than 47.21 lakh employers registered.
36.tq: Distinguish lakh and crore scales before comparing the numerical options.

36.s: Recognition of Prior Learning under PMKVY is intended to:
o: Provide working capital to street vendors
Certify existing skills against the National Skills Qualifications Framework
Provide EPF support for new formal jobs
36.x: Recognition of Prior Learning certifies skills that individuals already possess against the National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF).
36.tq: Identify the scheme by the action it performs—assessment and certification of existing skills.

36.s:

36.s: PMEGP met its target of creating how many new micro-enterprises, with what indicated distribution?

EPF-linked incentives for new formal jobs
Certification of artisan skills under NSQF

45.s: Which of the following correctly describes the sowing and harvesting period of Kharif crops?

o: The Commission recommended C2+50 per cent, whereas the Government uses 1.5 times A2+FL.
The Commission recommended MSP for 22 crops, whereas the Government has no crop coverage.
The Commission recommended 1.5 times A2+FL, whereas the Government uses C2+50 per cent.
Both recommend only A2+FL without any addition.
51.x: The National Commission on Farmers recommended MSP at C2 plus 50 per cent, while the Government MSP policy uses 1.5 times A2+FL. MSPs are stated to cover 22 mandated crops.
51.tq: Split the paired cost concepts first: C2+50 per cent belongs to the Commission recommendation, while 1.5 times A2+FL belongs to current policy.
51.sec: National Commission on Agriculture and National Commission on Farmers  [APPSC]

51.s: Under PM-AASHA, which component involves procurement by NAFED and NCCF?
51.x: The Price Support Scheme (PSS) under PM-AASHA involves procurement through agencies such as NAFED and NCCF.
51.tq: Discriminate among similarly abbreviated PM-AASHA components by matching each one with its specific function.
51.sec: Schemes for better price realisation - PM-AASHA, e-NAM, Operation Greens  [APPSC]

51.s:
Consider the following statements about PM-AASHA:
1. It was launched in 2018 to provide remunerative prices.
2. Under PDPS, the price-gap coverage was raised to 40 per cent of State oilseed output.
3. Under MIS, the coverage mentioned is 25 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
51.x: PM-AASHA was launched in 2018. Its components include PDPS, with coverage raised to 40 per cent of State oilseed output, and MIS with 25 per cent coverage as specified.
51.tq: Retain the numerical pair 40 per cent and 25 per cent while testing the scheme’s objective and components together.
51.sec: Schemes for better price realisation - PM-AASHA, e-NAM, Operation Greens  [APPSC]

51.s: The e-NAM platform was launched in April 2016 by which organisation?
51.x: e-NAM was launched in April 2016 by the Small Farmers’ Agribusiness Consortium (SFAC).
51.tq: Use the launching agency as the decisive clue in a scheme–institution question.
51.sec: Schemes for better price realisation - PM-AASHA, e-NAM, Operation Greens  [APPSC]

51.s: As of March 2026, the e-NAM network covered:
o: 1,656 mandis in 23 States and 4 Union Territories
1,656 mandis in 22 States and 5 Union Territories
1,856 mandis in 24 States and 3 Union Territories
1,565 mandis in 23 States and 4 Union Territories
51.x: The e-NAM network was stated to cover 1,656 mandis across 23 States and 4 Union Territories as of March 2026.
51.tq: Treat the mandi, State and Union Territory figures as a single numerical combination and reject altered digits or coverage.
51.sec: Schemes for better price realisation - PM-AASHA, e-NAM, Operation Greens  [APPSC]

51.s: Operation Greens was initially intended to stabilise the prices of which group of commodities?
51.x: Operation Greens initially focused on stabilising Tomato–Onion–Potato prices, on the lines of Operation Flood.
51.tq: Recall the distinctive TOP acronym and avoid substituting other agricultural commodity groups.
51.sec: Schemes for better price realisation - PM-AASHA, e-NAM, Operation Greens  [APPSC]

51.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding Operation Greens?
o: It transports perishables by air under the Price Support Scheme.
It was limited permanently to tomato, onion and potato.
It was provided for in Budget 2018–19 and was widened to 22 perishables from 2021–22.
It was launched in April 2016 and initially covered all cereals.
51.x: Operation Greens was included in Budget 2018–19 and, from 2021–22, was widened from the original TOP commodities to 22 perishables.
51.tq: Find the option that preserves both the initial policy year and the later expansion instead of an absolute limitation.
51.sec: Schemes for better price realisation - PM-AASHA, e-NAM, Operation Greens  [APPSC]

51.s: The primary purpose of Krishi UDAN is to:
o: Transport perishables by air to raise value realisation
Create a unified electronic APMC platform
Provide crop insurance to tenant farmers
51.x: Krishi UDAN uses air transport for perishables with the objective of improving value realisation.
51.tq: Identify the scheme from its operational instrument—air transport—rather than from a general price-support objective.
51.sec: Schemes for better price realisation - PM-AASHA, e-NAM, Operation Greens  [APPSC]

51.s:
With reference to the Andhra Pradesh Agriculture Budget for 2026–27, consider the following statements:
1. Its approximate outlay was ₹53,753 crore.
2. The Agriculture Department allocation was ₹12,153 crore.
3. Agriculture accounted for 33.20 per cent of GSDP.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
51.x: The 2026–27 Andhra Pradesh Agriculture Budget had an approximate outlay of ₹53,753 crore, included ₹12,153 crore for the Agriculture Department, and represented 33.20 per cent of GSDP.
51.tq: Verify the three figures independently, since the distractors alter either the allocation, total outlay or GSDP share.
51.sec: AP agriculture support - agriculture budget, PM-KISAN, Annadata Sukhibhava  [APPSC]

51.s: The 2026–27 separate Agriculture Budget of Andhra Pradesh was the third such budget and was presented by:
51.x: The 2026–27 Agriculture Budget was the third separate Agriculture Budget of Andhra Pradesh and was presented by Minister K. Atchannaidu.
51.tq: Link the State budget sequence with the responsible Minister, not with chairs of national commissions.
51.sec: AP agriculture support - agriculture budget, PM-KISAN, Annadata Sukhibhava  [APPSC]

51.s: Which one of the following correctly describes PM-KISAN?
o: A Central Sector scheme providing ₹6,000 annually in three instalments of ₹2,000 to landholding families
A Central Sector scheme providing ₹20,000 annually in two instalments to all rural households
A State scheme providing ₹13,500 annually to tenant farmers only
A procurement scheme providing MSP compensation to oilseed producers
51.x: PM-KISAN is a Central Sector scheme, operative from 1 December 2018, that provides ₹6,000 per year in three instalments of ₹2,000 to eligible landholding farmer families.
51.tq: Separate PM-KISAN’s amount, instalment pattern and beneficiary category from State farmer-support schemes.
51.sec: AP agriculture support - agriculture budget, PM-KISAN, Annadata Sukhibhava  [APPSC]

51.s: The cut-off date for identifying landholding families under PM-KISAN was:
51.x: The cut-off date specified for identifying landholding families under PM-KISAN was 1 February 2019.
51.tq: Distinguish the scheme’s commencement date from its beneficiary-identification cut-off date.
51.sec: AP agriculture support - agriculture budget, PM-KISAN, Annadata Sukhibhava  [APPSC]

51.s: The 23rd instalment of PM-KISAN reached approximately how many farmers, with total disbursement exceeding which amount?
51.x: The 23rd instalment reached 9.49 crore farmers, and cumulative transfers exceeded ₹4.47 lakh crore.
51.tq: Pair the beneficiary count with the cumulative financial figure and reject reversals of units or digits.
51.sec: AP agriculture support - agriculture budget, PM-KISAN, Annadata Sukhibhava  [APPSC]

51.s: Under Annadata Sukhibhava–PM Kisan in Andhra Pradesh, the total annual assistance per family is:
51.x: The combined annual assistance is ₹20,000 per family, consisting of ₹14,000 from Andhra Pradesh and ₹6,000 from the Centre.
51.tq: Add the State and Central components before choosing the combined annual assistance.
51.sec: AP agriculture support - agriculture budget, PM-KISAN, Annadata Sukhibhava  [APPSC]

51.s: Which of the following correctly gives the instalment pattern under Annadata Sukhibhava–PM Kisan?
51.x: The instalments are ₹7,000 for Kharif, ₹7,000 for Rabi and ₹6,000 for Summer; each includes ₹2,000 from the Central component.
51.tq: Use the seasonal sequence to distinguish the two equal instalments from the smaller summer instalment.
51.sec: AP agriculture support - agriculture budget, PM-KISAN, Annadata Sukhibhava  [APPSC]

51.s:
Consider the following statements about Annadata Sukhibhava–PM Kisan:
1. It covers landholders and tenant farmers.
2. Tenant farmers are outside the coverage of PM-KISAN.
3. In 2025–26, it covered 46.86 lakh families with ₹6,309 crore released in two instalments.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
51.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct for Annadata Sukhibhava–PM Kisan. Statement 2 is also true only in relation to PM-KISAN itself, but it conflicts with the first statement when the combined Andhra Pradesh scheme is being described; the stated combined scheme covers tenant farmers, while tenants are outside PM-KISAN.
51.tq: Separate the beneficiary coverage of the combined State scheme from the narrower coverage of PM-KISAN.
51.sec: AP agriculture support - agriculture budget, PM-KISAN, Annadata Sukhibhava  [APPSC]

51.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Operation Greens — ₹20,000 per family per year to landless labourers
YSR Rythu Bharosa — ₹13,500 per family per year, including tenant and RoFR farmers
PM-KISAN — ₹13,500 per family per year, including tenant farmers
Annadata Sukhibhava — ₹6,000 per family per year without a State component
51.x: Earlier YSR Rythu Bharosa provided ₹13,500 per family per year and included tenant and RoFR farmers. The other options wrongly attribute amounts or objectives to unrelated schemes.
51.tq: Use beneficiary coverage and annual amount together to identify the correctly matched State scheme.
51.sec: AP agriculture support - agriculture budget, PM-KISAN, Annadata Sukhibhava  [APPSC]

51.s: The Ashok Dalwai Committee on Doubling Farmers’ Income functioned during:
51.x: The Ashok Dalwai Committee functioned during 2016–18 and produced 14 volumes. The target year for doubling farmers’ income was 2022, with 2015–16 as the base year.
51.tq: Keep the committee’s functioning period separate from its base year and target year.
51.sec: Doubling Farmers' Income - committee, sources of growth, target year

51.s: The target year and base year associated with the Doubling Farmers’ Income strategy were, respectively:
51.x: The strategy set 2022 as the target year and used 2015–16 as the base year.
51.tq: Read the pair in the order asked—target year first and base year second—to avoid reversing them.
51.sec: Doubling Farmers' Income - committee, sources of growth, target year

51.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the identified sources of growth in farmers’ income?
o: Exclusive dependence on traditional low-value crops
51.x: The seven sources include crop productivity, livestock productivity, resource-use efficiency, cropping intensity, diversification to high-value crops, better price realisation and movement to non-farm jobs. Exclusive dependence on traditional low-value crops is not one of them.
51.tq: Find the option that contradicts the diversification and productivity-based approach.
51.sec: Doubling Farmers' Income - committee, sources of growth, target year

51.s: The Doubling Farmers’ Income approach represents a shift from production-oriented thinking towards:
o: Income enhancement through value addition, market reform and post-harvest infrastructure
Withdrawal of livestock and fisheries from farm planning
51.x: The approach shifts from “production” to “income” through value addition, clusters, e-NAM and APMC reform, post-harvest infrastructure, livestock-fisheries integration and land-leasing laws.
51.tq: In an application question, identify the option that combines the stated income-enhancing interventions rather than a single production measure.
51.sec: Doubling Farmers' Income - committee, sources of growth, target year

51.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the seven sources of growth in farmers’ income?
51.x: The strategy identifies a shift to non-farm jobs as a source of income growth; reduction of non-farm employment opportunities is therefore not included.
51.tq: Watch for the reversed meaning in the option: the strategy supports a shift to non-farm jobs, not its reduction.
51.sec: Doubling Farmers' Income - committee, sources of growth, target year

51.s: According to the Union Budget 2026–27 figure cited for agriculture, the allocation was approximately:
51.x: The Union Budget 2026–27 allocated ₹1.3 lakh crore to agriculture, representing a 2.6 per cent increase.
51.tq: Distinguish the Union agriculture allocation from the separate Andhra Pradesh budget and scheme-specific figures.
51.sec: Universal angles

51.s: Farm unions criticised the Union Budget 2026–27 primarily for the absence of:
o: Oil palm cultivation and fisheries integration
51.x: Farm unions criticised the absence of statutory MSP and debt relief in the Union Budget 2026–27.
51.tq: Identify the specific criticism rather than selecting general agricultural policy measures.
51.sec: Universal angles

51.s:
Consider the following statements regarding oil palm cultivation in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Andhra Pradesh leads India in oil palm area.
2. Its oil palm area was 2.49 lakh hectares, constituting 48 per cent of India’s area.
3. Production of fresh fruit bunches was 22.81 lakh metric tonnes in 2024–25.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
51.x: Andhra Pradesh leads India in oil palm cultivation, with 2.49 lakh hectares or 48 per cent of India’s area, and produced 22.81 lakh metric tonnes of fresh fruit bunches in 2024–25.
51.tq: Check the leadership claim, area share and production figure as separate components of the State’s oil-palm position.
51.sec: Universal angles

51.s: Which of the following correctly describes Andhra Pradesh’s agricultural growth objective mentioned in the material?
o: 30 per cent growth in one year through 22 growth engines
48 per cent agricultural growth in five years through 17 growth engines
17 per cent growth in five years through 30 growth engines
30 per cent agricultural growth in five years through 17 growth engines
51.x: Andhra Pradesh has set a target of 30 per cent agricultural growth in five years through 17 growth engines.
51.tq: Keep the two figures attached to their correct units—30 per cent is the growth target and 17 is the number of growth engines.
