52.s: According to the Agricultural Census 2015-16, what proportion of total operational holdings and operated area respectively was accounted for by small and marginal holdings below 2 hectares?
52.x: Small and marginal holdings constituted 86.2% of all holdings but accounted for only 47.3% of the operated area in 2015-16.
52.tq: Read the table row-wise and distinguish the share of holdings from the share of operated area.
52.sec: Small and marginal holdings viability - holdings vs operated area, collective farming, FPOs  [APPSC]

52.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Agricultural Census 2015-16:
1. Small and marginal holdings constituted 86.2% of the holdings.
2. Semi-medium and medium holdings accounted for 43.6% of the operated area.
3. Semi-medium and medium holdings constituted 43.6% of the total holdings.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Semi-medium and medium holdings constituted 13.2% of holdings, not 43.6%; 43.6% was their share of operated area.
52.tq: Separate percentages referring to holdings from those referring to operated area.
52.sec: Small and marginal holdings viability - holdings vs operated area, collective farming, FPOs  [APPSC]

52.s: With reference to the Agricultural Census 2010-11, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Small holdings constituted about 85% of holdings and held about 58% of operated area.
Small holdings constituted about 58% of holdings and held about 44% of operated area.
Small holdings constituted about 85% of holdings and held about 44% of operated area.
Small holdings constituted about 44% of holdings and held about 85% of operated area.
52.x: In the 2010-11 Agricultural Census, small holdings were about 85% of holdings but accounted for only about 44% of the operated area.
52.tq: Match the two percentages with their correct dimensions instead of reversing the table.
52.sec: Small and marginal holdings viability - holdings vs operated area, collective farming, FPOs  [APPSC]

52.s:
Consider the following statements about agricultural holdings in India:
1. There were about 146 million holdings in 2015-16.
2. The average size of a holding was about 1.08 hectares in 2015-16.
3. The 11th Agriculture Census 2021-22 has, so far, only provisional State results.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: All three statements are correct: India had about 146 million holdings averaging 1.08 hectares in 2015-16, while only provisional State results of the 2021-22 Census were available as stated.
52.tq: Check each numerical and status statement independently before selecting the combined option.
52.sec: Small and marginal holdings viability - holdings vs operated area, collective farming, FPOs  [APPSC]

52.s: With reference to the provisional 11th Agriculture Census data for Andhra Pradesh, which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Average holding size—0.86 hectares; number of holdings—96.90 lakh
Average holding size—0.94 hectares; number of holdings—96.90 lakh
Average holding size—0.86 hectares; number of holdings—85.24 lakh
Average holding size—1.08 hectares; number of holdings—146 million
52.x: The provisional Andhra Pradesh figures are an average holding size of 0.86 hectares and 96.90 lakh holdings, compared with 0.94 hectares and 85.24 lakh holdings in 2015-16.
52.tq: Use the sure numerical pair and reject options that mix figures from different years or geographical levels.
52.sec: Small and marginal holdings viability - holdings vs operated area, collective farming, FPOs  [APPSC]

52.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a reason for the poor viability of small and marginal agricultural holdings?
52.x: Small and marginal holdings are associated with few surpluses, not abundant marketable surpluses. Uneconomical mechanisation, weak bargaining power and poor credit are identified viability constraints.
52.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated condition rather than merely naming a related problem.
52.sec: Small and marginal holdings viability - holdings vs operated area, collective farming, FPOs  [APPSC]

52.s: Which of the following measures is most directly intended to improve the viability and bargaining position of small and marginal farmers by aggregating them into producer organisations?
o: Reduction of operated area per holding
Replacement of crop insurance by informal lending
52.x: Farmer Producer Organisations aggregate farmers and improve their collective bargaining and economic position. The other alternatives would weaken, rather than improve, viability.
52.tq: Identify the institutional remedy that addresses fragmentation and weak bargaining power.
52.sec: Small and marginal holdings viability - holdings vs operated area, collective farming, FPOs  [APPSC]

52.s: The Central Sector scheme for formation and promotion of how many Farmer Producer Organisations was launched in 2020, with an outlay of ₹6,865 crore?
52.x: The 10,000 FPO scheme was launched in 2020 with an outlay of ₹6,865 crore.
52.tq: Use the scheme’s distinctive target number and expenditure together.
52.sec: Small and marginal holdings viability - holdings vs operated area, collective farming, FPOs  [APPSC]

52.s: As reported up to January 2026, how many farmers had been registered under the 10,000 FPO scheme?
52.x: By January 2026, 56.32 lakh farmers had been registered under the 10,000 FPO scheme.
52.tq: Distinguish lakh-level registration data from the number of holdings and the scheme target.
52.sec: Small and marginal holdings viability - holdings vs operated area, collective farming, FPOs  [APPSC]

52.s: Which of the following set of measures is associated with improving the viability of small and marginal holdings?
o: Reduction of irrigation and removal of collective institutions
Exclusive dependence on individual machinery ownership and informal credit
Custom Hiring Centres, cluster farming and cooperative or joint farming
Abolition of producer organisations and cluster-based activities
52.x: Custom Hiring Centres, cluster farming and cooperative or joint farming are identified as remedies for the viability constraints of small holdings.
52.tq: Select the option containing the complete set of stated institutional and operational remedies.
52.sec: Small and marginal holdings viability - holdings vs operated area, collective farming, FPOs  [APPSC]

52.s: Which one of the following statements regarding cooperative joint farming in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: There are 210 primary Cooperative Joint Farming Societies, while their federations are under liquidation.
There are 10,000 primary societies functioning under the FPO scheme.
There are 85.24 primary societies, while federations are being expanded.
There are 210 federations, while all primary societies have been dissolved.
52.x: Andhra Pradesh has 210 primary Cooperative Joint Farming Societies, while the federations are under liquidation as reported for 2024-25.
52.tq: Match the correct institutional level with the correct status instead of swapping societies and federations.
52.sec: Small and marginal holdings viability - holdings vs operated area, collective farming, FPOs  [APPSC]

52.s: The principal source for official data on farmer and agricultural labourer suicides in India is which of the following?
o: Situation Assessment Survey of Agricultural Households
Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India
52.x: The National Crime Records Bureau publishes the report titled “Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India” (ADSI), which is the cited source for these suicide data.
52.tq: Identify the exact official report title rather than a related agricultural publication.
52.sec: Farmer suicides - NCRB ADSI data, causes, states, AP position  [APPSC]

52.s: According to the NCRB ADSI 2015 data, the biggest reported cause of farmer suicides was:
52.x: The biggest cause identified in the NCRB ADSI 2015 data was bankruptcy or indebtedness.
52.tq: Recall the principal causal category and avoid substituting a general agricultural problem for the recorded cause.
52.sec: Farmer suicides - NCRB ADSI data, causes, states, AP position  [APPSC]

52.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the regional pattern of farmer suicides:
1. A 28-year NCRB analysis covered the period 1995-2023.
2. The analysis found a sharp resurgence in suicides in 2023 after a decade of decline.
3. Suicides have been concentrated mainly in rain-fed belts.
4. Historically, Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh have been among the most severely affected areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: All four statements correctly describe the reported time span, recent resurgence, rain-fed concentration and historical concentration in Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh.
52.tq: Combine temporal, geographical and state-level clues only after checking each statement.
52.sec: Farmer suicides - NCRB ADSI data, causes, states, AP position  [APPSC]

52.s: According to NCRB ADSI 2024, the total number of suicides reported in India and the number attributed to the farm sector respectively were:
52.x: ADSI 2024 reported 1,70,746 suicides in total, of which 10,546 belonged to the farm sector.
52.tq: Distinguish the aggregate total from the farm-sector subset.
52.sec: Farmer suicides - NCRB ADSI data, causes, states, AP position  [APPSC]

52.s: The farm-sector suicide figure of 10,546 in NCRB ADSI 2024 comprised:
o: 10,546 farmers or cultivators and no agricultural labourers
4,481 farmers or cultivators and 152 agricultural labourers
4,633 farmers or cultivators and 5,913 agricultural labourers
5,913 farmers or cultivators and 4,633 agricultural labourers
52.x: The farm-sector total consisted of 4,633 farmers or cultivators and 5,913 agricultural labourers.
52.tq: Break the aggregate into its two component categories before selecting the option.
52.sec: Farmer suicides - NCRB ADSI data, causes, states, AP position  [APPSC]

52.s: What percentage of total suicides did the farm sector account for in NCRB ADSI 2024?
52.x: The farm sector accounted for 10,546 out of 1,70,746 suicides, reported as 6.2% of the total.
52.tq: Link the percentage to the stated total and subset rather than to one component alone.
52.sec: Farmer suicides - NCRB ADSI data, causes, states, AP position  [APPSC]

52.s: With reference to the gender-wise distribution of farmer or cultivator suicides in NCRB ADSI 2024, which one of the following is correct?
52.x: Of the farmer or cultivator suicides, 4,481 were men and 152 were women.
52.tq: Keep the farmer or cultivator category separate from the broader farm-sector total.
52.sec: Farmer suicides - NCRB ADSI data, causes, states, AP position  [APPSC]

52.s: Which of the following correctly describes the reported position regarding farmer and tenant suicides in Andhra Pradesh under the coalition government?
o: The Tenant Farmers Association reported over 300 deaths, while 112 were officially recognised.
The Association reported 112 deaths, while over 300 were officially recognised.
No deaths were reported and no demand for an inquiry was made.
Both the Association and official records reported exactly 300 deaths.
52.x: The Tenant Farmers Association claimed that more than 300 farmers and tenants died by suicide, whereas only 112 were officially recognised. It demanded a truth-finding committee.

52.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the work of the National Commission on Farmers?
o: It was set up exclusively for food procurement and submitted one report in 2015.
It was set up to regulate foreign trade and submitted five reports during 1991-1996.
It was set up to formulate industrial policy and submitted two reports during 2007-2010.
It was set up to address the calamity of farmer suicides and submitted five reports during 2004-2006.
52.x: The Commission was established to address the crisis of farmer suicides and submitted five reports between 2004 and 2006.
52.tq: Match the Commission’s purpose with its correct number and period of reports.
52.sec: National Commission on Farmers (Swaminathan) - year, reports, MSP formula  [APPSC]

52.s:
C2, in the MSP formula recommended by the National Commission on Farmers, includes which of the following components?
1. A2 costs
2. Imputed value of family labour
3. Imputed rent and interest on owned land and capital
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: C2 includes A2, family labour and imputed rent and interest on owned land and capital; hence all three statements are correct.
52.tq: Expand the cost acronym component by component before judging the statements.

o: The Commission recommended C2 plus 50%, while the Government applies 50% over A2+FL.
The Commission recommended A2+FL plus 50%, while the Government applies C2 plus 50%.
The Commission recommended C2 minus 50%, while the Government applies A2 alone.

52.sec: National Commission on Farmers (Swaminathan) - year, reports, MSP formula  [APPSC]

Consider the following statements about the recommendations and vision of the National Commission on Farmers:
1. It supported land reforms and market reforms.
2. It recommended irrigation, cheaper institutional credit and crop insurance.
3. It envisaged farming as economically viable and ecologically sustainable.
4. It sought improvement in the quality of life of farmers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: All four statements reflect the Commission’s recommendations and core vision for economically viable, ecologically sustainable farming and improved farmer welfare.

52.x: The AP Land Licensed Cultivators Act, 2011 provided Loan Eligibility Cards (LECs) to tenant cultivators.

52.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Loan Eligibility Cards under the Andhra Pradesh Land Licensed Cultivators Act, 2011:
1. They facilitate access to credit for tenant cultivators.
2. They enable access to crop insurance.
3. They transfer ownership rights in the land to the tenant.

52.x: Loan Eligibility Cards facilitate credit and insurance for tenants without affecting the landowner's rights. They do not transfer ownership of the land.

CACP recommends MSP to the government.

57.s: Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay SanraksHan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA) was launched in which month and year?

all agricultural produce is procured by private agencies
agricultural exports are completely exempt from taxation
fertiliser subsidies reach only large farmers

57.s: A farmer sells an oilseed in the market below its MSP, but no physical procurement takes place. Under which PM-AASHA component may the farmer receive the difference between MSP and the market price in cash?
57.x: The Price Deficiency Payment Scheme (PDPS) makes a cash payment equal to the gap between MSP and the market price, mainly for oilseeds, without physical purchase.
57.tq: Apply the no-procurement and cash-payment distinction to the agricultural scenario.

PPSS — Private agencies procuring oilseeds at MSP in the original pilot

It was a 2018 pilot involving private stockists procuring oilseeds at MSP.

57.s: Which of the following commodities is covered under the Market Intervention Scheme (MIS) rather than the regular MSP list?

57.s:

57.x: MIS can be triggered by a price fall of at least 10% or a production rise of at least 10%. A production fall is not the stated trigger.

57.s: Under MIS, losses are ordinarily shared between the Centre and the States in which ratio?

o: Sugarcane Regulation Act, 1955 under the Agricultural Produce Markets Act
Essential Commodities (Sugarcane Pricing) Rules, 1966 under the Food Corporation of India Act
Sugarcane Development Act, 2009 under the National Food Security Act

57.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the State Advised Price (SAP) of sugarcane?
o: It is announced by some States, generally above FRP, for sugarcane purchased within those States.
It is a central price fixed by the FCI only for export-oriented sugar mills.

1. Wheat
2. Paddy
3. Pulses
4. Oilseeds

o: Pulses, oilseeds and copra are procured under PSS subject to a 25 per cent cap.
Coarse grains are procured exclusively by the FCI without State participation.
Cotton is procured under PSS with a ceiling of 25 per cent of production.

The Reserve Bank of India after approval of the CACP
Only the Cotton Corporation of India
District cooperative banks without central approval

57.tq: Ask which agency performs the function and which approval condition accompanies it.
57.sec: Procurement - open-ended vs limited procurement crops, decentralised procurement states, AP paddy procurement system

3. The Centre reimburses the economic cost after deducting the Central Issue Price.

o: The private sugar mills’ reserve stocks
Export through the WTO Food Reserve
57.x: Under the Paddy Procurement Scheme, Andhra Pradesh State agencies procure paddy for the FCI’s Central Pool.

Procure paddy so that farmers actually receive MSP

Perishable commodities not covered under MSP
Only wheat and paddy under open-ended procurement

57.s: The CACP’s price-recommendation framework seeks to provide farmers with a minimum margin over cost of approximately:
57.x: The factors considered by the CACP include a minimum 50 per cent margin over the cost of production.
57.tq: Test the exact percentage associated with the cost-plus margin principle.
57.sec: CACP - year set up, earlier name, factors considered

57.s:
Which of the following represents the composition of the CACP?
1. Chairman
2. Member Secretary
3. One official member
4. Two non-official members
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
57.x: The CACP consists of a Chairman, a Member Secretary, one official member and two non-official members.
57.tq: Check the full composition instead of confusing the number of members with the number of categories.
57.sec: CACP - year set up, earlier name, factors considered

57.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the regional and crop pattern of MSP procurement:
1. Actual procurement is concentrated mainly in paddy and wheat.
2. Procurement is concentrated in a few States, including Punjab, Haryana, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.
3. Eastern and North-Eastern farmers gain comparatively little from the existing procurement pattern.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
57.x: All three statements are correct. Procurement is concentrated in paddy and wheat and in a limited number of States, leaving many eastern and North-Eastern farmers with limited benefit.
57.tq: Combine crop bias and regional bias to identify the complete criticism.
57.sec: Criticism - regional and crop bias, Shanta Kumar Committee findings, legal guarantee demand

57.s: The Shanta Kumar High-Level Committee (2015) estimated that approximately what proportion of farmers sell to procurement agencies at MSP?
57.x: The Shanta Kumar Committee estimated that only about 6 per cent of farmers sell their produce to procurement agencies at MSP.
57.tq: Retain the committee’s low participation estimate against larger distractor percentages.
57.sec: Criticism - regional and crop bias, Shanta Kumar Committee findings, legal guarantee demand

57.s: Why is MSP for pulses, oilseeds and coarse grains often described as largely symbolic?
o: Their prices are fixed only by State governments.
Actual procurement of these crops is limited compared with paddy and wheat.
They are not agricultural commodities under Indian law.
They are legally excluded from the MSP system.
57.x: MSP is announced for these crops, but actual procurement is limited, making the support largely symbolic in practice.
57.tq: Distinguish announcement of a support price from effective procurement at that price.
57.sec: Criticism - regional and crop bias, Shanta Kumar Committee findings, legal guarantee demand

57.s: Farmer unions demanding a legal guarantee for MSP primarily seek a law that would:
o: Replace all MSP procurement with direct cash transfers
Bind procurement agencies to purchase eligible produce at MSP
Transfer the power to fix MSP from CACP to State governments
57.x: The legal-guarantee demand seeks to bind procurement at MSP. It does not automatically mean abolition of private trade or transfer of MSP powers to States.
57.tq: Identify the precise legal obligation sought rather than broader consequences or policy alternatives.
57.sec: Criticism - regional and crop bias, Shanta Kumar Committee findings, legal guarantee demand

57.s:
Economists have expressed concern that a statutory legal guarantee for MSP could:
1. Distort agricultural trade.
2. Entrench monoculture.
3. Create difficulties in relation to WTO norms.
4. Make deficiency-payment models such as PDPS unnecessary in every case.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
57.x: Economists warn that a legal MSP guarantee could distort trade, reinforce monoculture and create WTO-related concerns. They often prefer PDPS-type deficiency payments as an alternative; it would not necessarily become unnecessary.
57.tq: Spot the overstatement in the claim that one policy model makes all alternatives unnecessary.
57.sec: Criticism - regional and crop bias, Shanta Kumar Committee findings, legal guarantee demand

57.s: A plea seeking MSP at least equal to the weighted average cost of production led the Supreme Court to issue notice to the Centre in:
57.x: The Supreme Court issued notice to the Centre on such a plea on 14 April 2026.
57.tq: Use the exact date and issue to distinguish a judicial development from a policy recommendation.
57.sec: Criticism - regional and crop bias, Shanta Kumar Committee findings, legal guarantee demand

57.s: Wheat procurement during RMS 2026–27 was reported to be:
o: More than 35 million tonnes, exceeding the 34.5 million tonne target
34.5 million tonnes, exactly equal to the target
30 million tonnes, 17 per cent below the target
120.65 million tonnes, equal to total output
57.x: More than 35 million tonnes of wheat were procured during RMS 2026–27, exceeding the 34.5 million tonne target. The previous year’s procurement was 30 million tonnes.
57.tq: Separate procurement, target and total output figures before choosing the correct quantitative statement.
57.sec: Procurement - open-ended vs limited procurement crops, decentralised procurement states, AP paddy procurement system

57.s: Which pair of States led wheat procurement during RMS 2026–27, with approximately 12.1 million tonnes and 10.4 million tonnes respectively?
57.x: Punjab procured approximately 12.1 million tonnes and Madhya Pradesh approximately 10.4 million tonnes, making them the leading States in the reported procurement figures.
57.tq: Match the leading States with their approximate procurement quantities.
57.sec: Procurement - open-ended vs limited procurement crops, decentralised procurement states, AP paddy procurement system

57.s:
The period from 1950 to 1965 in the agricultural development of India is associated with which of the following?
1. Land reforms
2. Community development
3. Expansion of irrigation
4. Introduction of Bt cotton for commercial cultivation
Which of the statements given above are correct?
57.x: The Pre-Green Revolution phase, from 1950 to 1965, focused on land reforms, community development and irrigation expansion. Bt cotton was approved much later, in 2002.
57.tq: Separate the characteristics of the Pre-Green Revolution phase from later technological developments.
57.sec: Phases of Indian agricultural development

57.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Phase of agricultural development — Hallmark

1. Green Revolution phase — HYV wheat and rice
2. Price-support and procurement phase — PDS distribution at issue price
3. Post-1991 phase — Direct income support through PM-KISAN
4. Pre-Green Revolution phase — WTO membership

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
57.x: HYV wheat and rice marked the Green Revolution phase; PDS distribution at issue price marked the price-support and procurement phase; and PM-KISAN belongs to the post-1991 reform phase. WTO membership occurred in the post-1991 period, not the Pre-Green Revolution period.
57.tq: Match each phase with its distinctive hallmark and reject the misplaced WTO reference.
57.sec: Phases of Indian agricultural development

57.s:
Consider the following events:
A. Establishment of APC and FCI
B. WTO membership of India
C. Release of the Wheat Revolution stamp
D. Beginning of the Pre-Green Revolution phase
Which of the following is the correct chronological order?
57.x: The Pre-Green Revolution phase began in 1950, APC and FCI were set up in 1965, the Wheat Revolution stamp was released in July 1968, and India became a WTO member in 1995.
57.tq: Use the dates 1950, 1965, 1968 and 1995 to fix the sequence.
57.sec: Phases of Indian agricultural development

57.s: The Wheat Revolution stamp associated with Indian agriculture was released in:
57.x: The Wheat Revolution stamp was released in July 1968 during the Green Revolution phase.
57.tq: Test the exact month and year attached to a distinctive historical agricultural event.
57.sec: Phases of Indian agricultural development

57.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the price-support and procurement phase of Indian agricultural development?
o: Distribution through PDS at issue price
MSP and buffer stocks maintained by FCI
57.x: Direct income support through PM-KISAN is associated with the post-1991 phase. The price-support and procurement phase involved MSP, FCI buffer stocks, procurement from surplus States and PDS distribution at issue price.
57.tq: Find the item belonging to the post-1991 reform phase rather than the procurement phase.
57.sec: Phases of Indian agricultural development

57.s:
In the WTO Agreement on Agriculture, which of the following is included in the Green Box?
1. Agricultural research
2. Disease control
3. Infrastructure
4. Decoupled income support
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
57.x: The Green Box covers measures considered not to distort trade, including research, disease control, infrastructure, food security and decoupled income support.
57.tq: Identify the common principle linking the non-trade-distorting Green Box measures.
57.sec: Agricultural policy since 1991 - WTO AoA, input subsidies, GM crops, trade liberalisation

57.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Blue Box support under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture?
o: Support exclusively for infrastructure and disease control
Income support completely unrelated to production
Direct payments tied to limiting production
All support exceeding the de minimis limit
57.x: Blue Box measures consist of direct payments linked to programmes that limit production.
57.tq: Discriminate between the production-limiting Blue Box and the non-distorting Green Box.
57.sec: Agricultural policy since 1991 - WTO AoA, input subsidies, GM crops, trade liberalisation

57.s:
With reference to the Amber Box under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture, consider the following statements:
1. It includes MSP and input subsidies.
2. Power, fertiliser, seed and irrigation subsidies may fall under it.
3. The de minimis limit is 5 per cent for developed countries and 10 per cent for developing countries.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
57.x: Amber Box support includes trade-distorting support such as MSP and input subsidies for power, fertiliser, seed and irrigation. The de minimis limits are 5 per cent for developed countries and 10 per cent for developing countries.
57.tq: Combine the category, examples and numerical thresholds before selecting the coded option.
57.sec: Agricultural policy since 1991 - WTO AoA, input subsidies, GM crops, trade liberalisation

57.s: Which of the following best describes the agricultural impact of India’s WTO entry in 1995 as stated in the context of farm incomes?
o: Subsidies rose as a share of farm income and import competition declined.
Subsidies fell as a share of farm income while import competition increased.
Real farm incomes doubled because of increased import competition.
Both subsidies and import competition declined steadily.
57.x: After WTO entry in 1995, subsidies declined as a share of farm income while import competition increased.
57.tq: Test the direction of two simultaneous trends rather than recalling only one trend.
57.sec: Agricultural policy since 1991 - WTO AoA, input subsidies, GM crops, trade liberalisation

57.s: Input costs for fertiliser, seed and pesticide are stated to have risen by more than what percentage since the early 2000s, while real farm incomes stagnated?
57.x: Input costs for fertiliser, seed and pesticide rose by over 300 per cent since the early 2000s, while real farm incomes stagnated.
57.tq: Use the quantitative threshold directly and distinguish ‘over 300 per cent’ from nearby rounded figures.
57.sec: Agricultural policy since 1991 - WTO AoA, input subsidies, GM crops, trade liberalisation

57.s: Which genetically modified crop was approved for commercial cultivation in India in 2002?
57.x: Bt cotton, approved in 2002, is the only genetically modified crop identified as approved for commercial cultivation in India.
57.tq: Use the crop-year pair to distinguish the approved GM crop from unapproved alternatives.
57.sec: Agricultural policy since 1991 - WTO AoA, input subsidies, GM crops, trade liberalisation

57.s: Farmer groups’ principal concern regarding India-U.S. trade agreements and other FTAs is their possible effect on:
57.x: Farmer groups fear that the India-U.S. trade deal and other FTAs may adversely affect agriculture through increased trade competition.
57.tq: Apply the trade-policy concern to the sector directly identified as vulnerable.
57.sec: Agricultural policy since 1991 - WTO AoA, input subsidies, GM crops, trade liberalisation

57.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the legal status of Minimum Support Price in India?
o: It is a constitutional right of every farmer.
It is an administrative decision and is not presently a legal right.
It is a judicially enforceable right under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture.
It is a statutory entitlement enforceable against every private buyer.
57.x: MSP is an administrative decision rather than a legal right. Farmer organisations have demanded that it be given a legal guarantee.
57.tq: Distinguish the existing administrative mechanism from the demand for a future legal guarantee.
57.sec: MSP debate - legal guarantee, Swaminathan formula, concentration, export bans

57.s: The National Commission on Farmers, popularly associated with the Swaminathan Commission, was constituted in:
57.x: The National Commission on Farmers was constituted in 2004 and submitted five reports during 2004–06.
57.tq: Link the commission’s establishment year with its report period to avoid confusing it with the 1991 reforms.
57.sec: MSP debate - legal guarantee, Swaminathan formula, concentration, export bans

57.s:
Consider the following statements about the Swaminathan Commission:
1. It submitted five reports.
2. Its reports were submitted during 2004–06.
3. It recommended MSP at C2 plus 50 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
57.x: The Swaminathan Commission submitted five reports between 2004 and 2006 and recommended MSP at C2 plus 50 per cent.
57.tq: Check the commission’s report count, period and formula together.
57.sec: MSP debate - legal guarantee, Swaminathan formula, concentration, export bans

57.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the government’s MSP formula from the Swaminathan Commission’s recommendation?
o: The government applies 50 per cent over A2+FL, whereas the Commission recommended C2+50 per cent.
The government applies 50 per cent over C2, whereas the Commission recommended A2+FL.
Both apply 50 per cent over A2+FL.
Both apply 50 per cent over C2.
57.x: The Swaminathan Commission recommended C2+50 per cent, whereas the government applies 50 per cent over A2+FL.
57.tq: Split the options by identifying the cost base—A2+FL or C2—before considering the 50 per cent margin.
57.sec: MSP debate - legal guarantee, Swaminathan formula, concentration, export bans

57.s: According to the SKM’s C2+50 per cent calculation, what should have been the paddy MSP for 2026–27, compared with the notified MSP of ₹2,441 per quintal?
57.x: The SKM stated that the paddy MSP should have been ₹3,243 per quintal under the C2+50 per cent formula, against the fixed ₹2,441.
57.tq: Compare the demanded formula-based figure with the notified figure rather than calculating a new value.
57.sec: MSP debate - legal guarantee, Swaminathan formula, concentration, export bans

57.s: The SKM called for village protests concerning the 2026–27 paddy MSP during which period?
57.x: The SKM called village protests for 27–31 May 2026 over the paddy MSP issue.
57.tq: Test the exact date range associated with the MSP protest call.
57.sec: MSP debate - legal guarantee, Swaminathan formula, concentration, export bans

57.s:
Economists have argued that a legal guarantee for MSP could have which of the following consequences?
1. Distortion of trade
2. Encouragement of monoculture
3. Breach of WTO norms
4. Elimination of fiscal costs
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
57.x: Economists have warned that a legal MSP may distort trade, encourage monoculture and breach WTO norms. It would not eliminate fiscal costs; fiscal cost is one of the concerns in the debate.
57.tq: Reject the absolute economic claim that a legal guarantee would eliminate fiscal costs.
57.sec: MSP debate - legal guarantee, Swaminathan formula, concentration, export bans

57.s:
Which of the following measures has been suggested as an alternative or complement to a universal legal MSP guarantee?
1. Wider procurement
2. Price-deficiency payments
3. Direct income support
4. Decentralised procurement
5. Digital procurement through e-NAM
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
57.x: The suggested approaches include wider procurement, price-deficiency payments through PM-AASHA, direct income support through PM-KISAN, decentralised procurement and digital procurement through e-NAM.
57.tq: Recognise the complete package of policy alternatives rather than selecting only the price-related measures.
57.sec: MSP debate - legal guarantee, Swaminathan formula, concentration, export bans

57.s: The Economic Survey 2025–26 suggested using savings from procurement efficiency to promote:
o: Exclusive cultivation of rice in surplus States
Compulsory replacement of all pulses by wheat
Voluntary crop diversification away from water-guzzling rice and wheat
57.x: The Economic Survey 2025–26 suggested using procurement-efficiency savings to fund voluntary crop diversification away from water-guzzling rice and wheat.
57.tq: Connect procurement savings with the stated environmental and cropping-pattern objective.
57.sec: MSP debate - legal guarantee, Swaminathan formula, concentration, export bans

57.s: Which of the following statements regarding the notified Kharif 2026–27 MSP is correct?
o: The MSPs were notified in January 2026 and paddy MSP was ₹3,243 per quintal.
The MSPs were notified in May 2025 and paddy MSP was ₹2,441 per quintal.
The MSPs were notified in May 2026 and paddy MSP was ₹2,441 per quintal.
The MSPs were notified in August 2026 and paddy MSP was ₹2,441 per quintal.
57.x: Kharif 2026–27 MSPs were notified in May 2026, with paddy MSP fixed at ₹2,441 per quintal.
57.tq: Pair the notification month and agricultural year with the exact paddy figure.
57.sec: Universal angles

57.s: Which one of the following correctly describes paddy procurement arrangements in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Paddy is bought on behalf of FCI with DBT within 48 hours, while DCMS and APMARKFED operate the cooperative channel.
Paddy is procured on behalf of WTO, while NABARD operates the cooperative channel.
Paddy procurement is confined to direct export and excludes FCI.
Paddy is bought only by private traders, with cash payment after 90 days.
57.x: Andhra Pradesh is a major procurement State. Paddy is procured on behalf of FCI, DBT is made within 48 hours, and DCMS and APMARKFED run the cooperative channel.
57.tq: Identify the responsible procurement agency, payment timeline and cooperative institutions together.
57.sec: Universal angles

57.s: Which of the following States is described as one of the top procurement States and a major paddy procurement State?
57.x: Andhra Pradesh is identified as one of the top procurement States and as a major State for paddy procurement.
57.tq: Use the State-specific procurement association to distinguish the AP angle.
57.sec: Universal angles

57.s: The wheat procurement figure reported as a record in June 2026 was:
57.x: Wheat procurement was reported to have crossed 35 million tonnes, constituting a record figure.
57.tq: Distinguish the reported procurement threshold from nearby rounded quantities.
57.sec: Universal angles

57.s: The sugarcane Fair and Remunerative Price for 2026–27 was raised by:
57.x: The sugarcane FRP was raised by ₹10 for the 2026–27 season.
57.tq: Recall the exact per-unit increase rather than confusing FRP with MSP.
57.sec: Universal angles

57.s:
Andhra Pradesh farm bodies protested in 2026 for MSP procurement of which of the following crops?
1. Maize
2. Pulses
3. Cotton
4. Tomato
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
57.x: The protests in Andhra Pradesh sought MSP procurement for maize, pulses, cotton and tomato.
57.tq: Test the complete crop list and avoid excluding the non-cereal items.
57.sec: Universal angles

57.s:
Which of the following correctly identifies the principal criticisms and debates surrounding MSP procurement?
1. A2+FL versus C2 as the cost base
2. Demand for a legal guarantee
3. WTO limits and fiscal cost
4. Regional imbalance in procurement
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
57.x: The central debates concern the appropriate cost base, legal enforceability, WTO constraints, fiscal cost and regional imbalance in procurement.
57.tq: Group the formula, legal, international, fiscal and regional dimensions of the MSP debate.
57.sec: Universal angles

58.s: The Food Corporation of India was set up on which date?
58.x: The Food Corporation of India was established on 14 January 1965.
58.tq: Use the precise day and year to distinguish the establishment date from the governing Act and digital-system dates.
58.sec: FCI - year set up, Act, recommending committee, missions and functions, digital systems (OSM, Anna Darpan)

58.s: The Food Corporation of India was established under which Act on the recommendation of which committee?
o: Food Corporations Act, 1964; Food Grains Prices Committee chaired by L. K. Jha
Essential Commodities Act, 1955; Agricultural Prices Commission
Agricultural Produce Markets Act; Kelkar Committee
58.x: FCI was set up under the Food Corporations Act, 1964, on the recommendation of the Food Grains Prices Committee associated with L. K. Jha in 1964.
58.tq: Match the statutory basis with the recommending committee instead of confusing the Food Corporations Act with other agriculture and food laws.
58.sec: FCI - year set up, Act, recommending committee, missions and functions, digital systems (OSM, Anna Darpan)

58.s: The headquarters of the Food Corporation of India is located at
58.x: The headquarters of the Food Corporation of India is in New Delhi.
58.tq: Test the institutional location directly and distinguish the FCI headquarters from the location of IGMRI.
58.sec: FCI - year set up, Act, recommending committee, missions and functions, digital systems (OSM, Anna Darpan)

58.s: With reference to the procurement role of the Food Corporation of India, which one of the following is correct?
o: It regulates agricultural markets under State APMC laws.
It distributes foodgrains without the participation of State agencies.
It is the nodal agency for procuring wheat and paddy under price support.
It procures only oilseeds and pulses under price support.
58.x: FCI is the nodal agency for procuring wheat and paddy under price support, with State agencies functioning alongside it. Regulation of agricultural markets is associated with State APMC laws.
58.tq: Identify the precise institutional responsibility and reject options that expand or wrongly transfer the agency’s role.
58.sec: FCI - year set up, Act, recommending committee, missions and functions, digital systems (OSM, Anna Darpan)

58.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the missions of the Food Corporation of India:
1. Efficient procurement of foodgrains at MSP.
2. Storage, movement and distribution of foodgrains.
3. Maintaining operational and buffer stocks for food security.
4. Making foodgrains accessible at reasonable prices to weaker sections through TPDS.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
58.x: All four statements describe the missions of FCI: procurement at MSP, storage and distribution, maintenance of operational and buffer stocks, and access to foodgrains through TPDS.
58.tq: Check whether each statement belongs to the agency’s stated mission before selecting the complete combination.
58.sec: FCI - year set up, Act, recommending committee, missions and functions, digital systems (OSM, Anna Darpan)

58.s: The Online Storage Management system of the Food Corporation of India was rolled out from
58.x: OSM was rolled out from 1 April 2022.
58.tq: Separate the rollout date of OSM from the establishment year of FCI and the date of the governing Act.
58.sec: FCI - year set up, Act, recommending committee, missions and functions, digital systems (OSM, Anna Darpan)

58.s: The principal purpose of the Online Storage Management (OSM) system is to facilitate
o: efficient storage, movement and distribution under TPDS
international trade in foodgrains through the WTO
regulation of agricultural markets by State governments
direct cash transfers to farmers under MSP
58.x: OSM was introduced for efficient storage, movement and distribution of foodgrains under the Targeted Public Distribution System.
58.tq: Link the digital tool to the operational stage it manages—storage, movement and distribution under TPDS.
58.sec: FCI - year set up, Act, recommending committee, missions and functions, digital systems (OSM, Anna Darpan)

58.s: Which of the following correctly describes Anna Darpan?
o: An agricultural market-regulation law administered by State APMCs
A foodgrain price committee chaired by L. K. Jha
An integrated supply-chain management system of FCI
A buffer-stock accounting system of the WTO
58.x: Anna Darpan is FCI’s integrated supply-chain management system, intended to modernise its supply chain. It belongs to the food and PDS side, not to the Agriculture Ministry.
58.tq: Discriminate between a digital FCI supply-chain system and institutions or laws dealing with agricultural markets and trade.
58.sec: FCI - year set up, Act, recommending committee, missions and functions, digital systems (OSM, Anna Darpan)

58.s:
With reference to Anna Darpan, consider the following statements:
1. It is associated with the food and PDS side of administration.
2. It is a system belonging to the Agriculture Ministry.
3. It is intended to modernise the supply chain of FCI.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
58.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Anna Darpan is associated with the food and PDS side and modernises FCI’s supply chain; it does not belong to the Agriculture Ministry.
58.tq: Spot the wrong-ministry trap while retaining the two statements that identify the system’s sector and purpose.
58.sec: FCI - year set up, Act, recommending committee, missions and functions, digital systems (OSM, Anna Darpan)

58.s: Which digital system provides end-to-end tracking of foodgrain from procurement to the Fair Price Shop, together with real-time stock monitoring to check leakage?
58.x: SARTHAK-PDS digitally tracks grain from procurement to the Fair Price Shop and monitors stocks in real time to help prevent leakage.
58.tq: Trace the system’s coverage from procurement to the FPS and use its anti-leakage function as the identifying clue.
58.sec: FCI - year set up, Act, recommending committee, missions and functions, digital systems (OSM, Anna Darpan)

58.s: The Indian Grain Storage Management and Research Institute, associated with foodgrain storage research and training, is situated at
58.x: The Indian Grain Storage Management and Research Institute is located at Hapur.
58.tq: Distinguish the research institute’s location from the headquarters of FCI and the names of persons associated with the recommending committee.
58.sec: FCI - year set up, Act, recommending committee, missions and functions, digital systems (OSM, Anna Darpan)

58.s:
Which of the following are identified as challenges faced by the Food Corporation of India?
1. Rising operating costs
2. Excess stocks and wastage
3. Falling issue-price earnings
4. Regulation of agricultural markets by FCI
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
58.x: Rising operating costs, excess stocks and wastage, and falling issue-price earnings are identified challenges of FCI. Regulation of agricultural markets is not an FCI function or challenge described here; it falls under State APMC laws.
58.tq: Separate genuine operational and financial challenges from a wrongly assigned institutional responsibility.
58.sec: FCI - year set up, Act, recommending committee, missions and functions, digital systems (OSM, Anna Darpan)

58.s:
Which one of the following correctly represents the sequence of major developments in India's Public Distribution System?
A. PDS — RPDS — TPDS — AAY
B. RPDS — PDS — AAY — TPDS
C. PDS — TPDS — RPDS — AAY
D. AAY — RPDS — TPDS — PDS
58.x: The sequence was PDS, followed by RPDS in June 1992, TPDS in June 1997 and AAY on 25 December 2000.
58.tq: Use the first-and-last items to eliminate reversed sequences.
58.sec: TPDS evolution - PDS, RPDS, TPDS, AAY (launch sequence), leakage estimates, reforms (ePoS, Aadhaar seeding, DBT)  [APPSC]

58.s: The Public Distribution System in India first began in the 1940s primarily in the context of which event?
o: The introduction of the National Food Security Act
58.x: Rationing began in the 1940s against the backdrop of the Bengal famine. The system was later revived during the food shortages of the 1960s.
58.tq: Identify the historical context associated with the origin of the policy.
58.sec: TPDS evolution - PDS, RPDS, TPDS, AAY (launch sequence), leakage estimates, reforms (ePoS, Aadhaar seeding, DBT)  [APPSC]

58.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Revamped Public Distribution System (RPDS):
1. It was launched in June 1992.
2. It focused on backward, hilly and drought-prone areas.
3. It introduced separate entitlements for BPL and APL households.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
58.x: RPDS was launched in June 1992 for backward, hilly and drought areas. Separate BPL and APL entitlements were introduced later under TPDS.
58.tq: Split the statements by matching each feature with the correct reform stage.
58.sec: TPDS evolution - PDS, RPDS, TPDS, AAY (launch sequence), leakage estimates, reforms (ePoS, Aadhaar seeding, DBT)  [APPSC]

58.s: Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS), introduced in June 1997, was characterised by which of the following?
o: Separate entitlements for BPL and APL households
Conversion of all fair price shops into mini-marts
58.x: TPDS introduced separate entitlements for Below Poverty Line and Above Poverty Line households in June 1997.
58.tq: Distinguish the defining feature of a policy from features of later reforms.
58.sec: TPDS evolution - PDS, RPDS, TPDS, AAY (launch sequence), leakage estimates, reforms (ePoS, Aadhaar seeding, DBT)  [APPSC]

58.s: Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) was launched on 25 December 2000 to provide how much foodgrain per family per month to the poorest households?
58.x: AAY was launched on 25 December 2000 for the poorest households, with an entitlement of 35 kg of foodgrain per family per month.
58.tq: Use the exact date and quantity rather than confusing AAY with other food entitlements.
58.sec: TPDS evolution - PDS, RPDS, TPDS, AAY (launch sequence), leakage estimates, reforms (ePoS, Aadhaar seeding, DBT)  [APPSC]

58.s: The National Food Security Act, 2013, provided a legal entitlement to foodgrain for approximately how many people?
58.x: The National Food Security Act, 2013, gave a legal food entitlement to about 800 million people.
58.tq: Test the scale of coverage through the exact approximate figure.
58.sec: TPDS evolution - PDS, RPDS, TPDS, AAY (launch sequence), leakage estimates, reforms (ePoS, Aadhaar seeding, DBT)  [APPSC]

58.s: Under the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY), NFSA foodgrains were made free from:
